I. Leunclavius <note>Johannes Leunclavius (1533–1594), a German historian and specialist in Ottoman history</note> in his Turkish nomenclature says: *Hunggiar* is a title of dignity attributed by the Turks to their Sultans, just as Roman Princes used to be called Emperors and Caesars, to be pronounced in only two syllables. *Franc-beg* means Italian Prince, or Prince of the Italians. Likewise, the Roman Pope is called by the Turks *Musulin Histor. 16.* <note>Reference to Leunclavius’s work 'Historiae Musulmanae Turcorum'</note> *Rum-beg*, Prince of Rome, or Lord of Rome. Thus in book 16 of the *Musulman History*, the Turks call the Roman Pope what the Persian ambassadors—sent last year while Sixtus V was still alive to solicit aid against the Turks—called *Rum Schach*, or King of Rome. *Rum Schach*, King of Rome: so the Roman Pope was called by the Persians. The same Leunclavius notes that *Megas Aphendis* <note>original Greek: Μέγας Αὐθέντης</note>, meaning Great Lord, is the name the Greeks use for the Sultan of the Turks; following the Italian custom, he is not called anything other than *The Grand Seignor* <note>original Italian: Il grand Seignor</note>.

The Tartars of today call the Pope and all Christians *Dezinthis*, which means Pagans, and *Chaur* <note>Likely 'Giaour', a derogatory term for non-Muslims</note>, that is to say infidels, Dogs, and Idolaters, because they honor wood and stones. This began after they were summoned by Pope Innocent IV to receive the Christian Religion. While they were almost inclined to do so, Satan stirred up the *Mahometans* <note>An archaic term for Muslims</note>, who did not want to lose such a choice morsel. They admonished them to take up the Religion of the *Alcoran* <note>The Quran</note> as the purest, insofar as it taught only the adoration of a single God, while that of the Christians was stuffed with idols. Furthermore, they argued their own religion was spirited and permitted everything to a free man, putting weapons in his hands, whereas the religion of Jesus Christ was only fit for the effeminate and people who ask for nothing but rest. These *Alcoranists* knew how to harangue so well that those who had no certain Religion embraced the worst one; leaving that law which is entirely spiritual, they seized the doctrine of the flesh, apostasy, and abomination around the year of grace 1247. In the Kingdom of Narsingue <note>The Vijayanagara Empire in Southern India</note>, the word *Gurupe* is a title of dignity, as one might say a learned and scholarly Priest; and the word *Delevay* as well, meaning Captain and General of the army, according to *F. P. du Jarric* <note>Pierre du Jarric (1566–1617), a Jesuit missionary and historian</note> in book 2, chapter 21 of his history of the East Indies. In the kingdom of Deccan, the word *Sabaio* is a title of dignity, meaning Captain of the King's personal guards; the word *Idalcan* <note>Likely 'Adil Khan', the title of the rulers of the Bijapur Sultanate</note> is another title of dignity, meaning the King’s lieutenant general throughout all his lands, according to the account of *Edward Barbosa* <note>Duarte Barbosa (c. 1480–1521), a Portuguese writer and explorer</note>, a Portuguese, in his summary of the Indies.

The person commissioned as *Toldan* by the King in the city of Pegu <note>In modern-day Myanmar</note>, the capital of the Kingdom of Pegu, has total authority. No one would dare present themselves before him without a gift, as it is the custom of the country not to approach one’s King, Prince, or Lord without acknowledging his power. But near the person of the King is the *Cobraim*, called *Mattacqui* by the Cathayans <note>People of Cathay, an old name for China</note>, who holds more credit than the *Toldans* and *Haozamants*, because he is the lieutenant general and acts as Regent throughout the entire country and Kingdom of Pegu. After the *Cobraim* and *Toldans* are the *Talcades*, which is to say Captains: one for the port of *Dogom* <note>Dagon, modern-day Yangon</note>, a day's journey from Pegu, and another for *Martaban*, four days away.

In the Island of Taprobane <note>An ancient geographical name, here identified with Sumatra</note> or Sumatra, there are among the Royal officers two of the most notable who oversee the entire state and civil order: namely, the general of the army whom they call *Nacauda-Roua*, that is to say, Royal Captain; and one named *Chambendure*, who is in charge of setting the price for all merchandise brought to the Island, and without whose license no one is so bold as to dare buy or sell, and who collects the tributes and taxes owed to the King. Modern Navigators, speaking of the names of the Kings and Princes of the West Indies, write the following: as the languages are different in the West Indies, the Lords of those countries also have various titles; in some places they are called *Queri*, in others *Caciques*, in certain parts *Tibà*, and in some others *Guasirò*. But for the most part, the word *Cacique* is of wide extent, and in many regions the sovereign Prince is called this. Those who are the next most wealthy and powerful after him, and who have a good number of vassals and subjects under them, are called *Sachò*. And just as these are subject to the *Cacique*, they also have under their jurisdiction Lords who possess lands and lordships, whom they call *Cabrâ*, who are like knights or simple Gentlemen distinguished from the common people, and have more authority than the commoners over whom they command. The lowliest can reach the honor of *Cabrâ* by behaving valiantly in war; for just as in our lands the King ennobles those who have conducted themselves as men of merit in combat and makes them knights of the accolade <note>A ceremony of knighthood involving a tap on the shoulder with a sword</note>, so the Cacique makes *Cabra* those who fight fiercely and are wounded in battle while performing some signal act, giving testimony of their bravery. From then on, they no longer mingle with the common people but are honored and respected, and their children succeed to the nobility of their fathers and are named *Cabrâ*, and consequently are obliged to go to war if the Cacique has need of their service. The greatest Lords are called *Morbichatz*. See Joseph de Acosta <note>A Spanish Jesuit missionary and naturalist (1540–1600)</note>, Book 5, Chapter 25, of his *History of the Indies*, treating the titles and dignities that existed among the Mexicans.

In China, the *Tutans* are absolute Governors of Provinces; after them are the *Ponchases*, and under those the *Anchases*; and the Constable or Master of the Men-at-Arms is called *Aitan*, and his Lieutenant *Luitilius*. Some write that there are five orders of dignity in this China: the first being the *Cunixes*, compared to our Princes and Counts, otherwise called *Toans*, as reported by Father Pietro Maffei <note>An Italian Jesuit historian (1533–1603)</note> in Book 6 of his *History of the Indies*.

## Of the Persians.

### CHAPTER XLVII.

->World / Age / Eternity <note>original Hebrew: "עולם"; Greek: "ἠλὼν αἰλὰν"</note><-

AELAM, Ailam, or Elam—meaning in the Hebrew language youth, or virgin, or hidden, or an age <note>The author is connecting the name Elam to various Hebrew words sharing the same root (CLM), such as "elem" (youth), "almah" (young woman), "alam" (to hide), and "olam" (eternity/world)</note>—the son of Shem, son of Noah (Genesis 10), was the one who first gave his name to the region of Persia. This region is not far distant from Mesopotamia, where Susa is situated, according to the testimony of Josephus in Book 1 of the *Antiquities of the Jews*, chapter 6, and of Strabo in Book 16. From this name, those Jews living in Elam or the region of Persia are called Elamites. Concerning this, the *Bundle of Myrrh* <note>original: "faisceau de myrrhe"; likely referring to the *Fasciculus Myrrhae*, a medieval devotional or historical commentary</note> reports that the Persians—descended from the blood and race of Japheth—and the Medes entered the region of the Elamites (successors of Aelan or Elam) and imposed the name of Persians upon them. This is confirmed by Benedictus Pererius <note>Benito Pereira (1535–1610), a Jesuit theologian and commentator</note> in his *Commentaries on the Book of Daniel*, Book 9. In fact, in Daniel chapter 8 and in the Acts of the Apostles chapter 2, we find this word "Elamites" being used to mean the Persians, because the Persians are close neighbors of the Medes. Xenophon even makes mention of the Elamite <note>original: "Ælamide"</note> tribe, which he takes to be Persians. In more ancient times, they were called the Elymaeans or Elymeans in Persia—those who were neighbors of the river Elee, or Tiritiri, who are currently called Azamians, and their region Elam. This word encompasses Susiana, what is properly Persia, and the land of the Parthians, as it was formerly like the patrimony of the Kings of Persia, according to the words of Ludovico di Varthema <note>referred to as "Louys Bartheme", a 15th-century Italian traveler</note> in his books of travels.

Today, the Persians or Persans bear the name of Azamians, as do the Parthians. The easternmost part of Persia is that of Molitene and Cabanden, currently Yezd <note>original: "Iecxt"</note> and Luristan <note>original: "Iurestan"</note>, all surrounded by mountains that are more spacious than others in Persia. It is a wonder of nature to see how these mountains form a pass like that of the Caspian Gates, or Thermopylae, which is also called the Gates of Susa. Through this pass, called Luristan, one enters the country of Persia; the place is so difficult that one can only pass through one after another. Josephus, in Book 1, chapter 6 of his *Antiquities*, writes that Shem, the son of Noah, had five children who possessed Asia from the Euphrates all the way to the Indian Ocean; for Elam left his blood to the Elamites, from whom the Persians are descended. But as for the name "Persian," it is not of such ancient origin, as it happened that the Persians were later called Pantheans, after a king bearing that name, then
<margin>Cephenians <note>original Greek: "κηφῆνες"</note></margin> Cephenians, and <margin>Artaeans <note>original Greek: "ἀρταῖοι"</note></margin> Artaeans, and finally Persians, from Perseus <note>original: "perse"</note>, son of Jupiter, according to the fables of the Greeks, as is written in Herodotus, Book 7 of his *Histories*. Along with him, one should consult Strabo, Books 15 and 16 of his *Geography*; Pliny, Book 6, chapter 27; Marco Polo the Venetian, Book 1 of his travels; Sir John Mandeville in his travels; Giosafat Barbaro in his travels in Persia, printed in Venice; and Messer Ambrogio Contarini, Ambassador of the Venetians, in his travels in Persia, also printed in Venice.

### *On the Persian Language.*
## CHAPTER XLVIII.

Plutarch, in the *Life of Themistocles*, and Valerius Maximus, in Book 8, Chapter 7, make a great deal of the fact—and hold it in high esteem—that this personage, Greek by nation, Themistocles, while a fugitive in the kingdom of Persia, learned to speak the Persian language within a year. Agathias and Suidas <note>a 10th-century Byzantine encyclopedia</note> would have us believe that it is recorded in the memoirs of the ancients that Khosrow <note>original: "Cosroes"</note>, King of Persia, had the works of the philosophers Plato and Aristotle translated from the Greek language into his own Persian tongue. This clearly demonstrates that this Persian language, in the time of that great Greek Captain and the aforementioned King Khosrow of Persia, was quite different and dissimilar from the Greek language.

Those who have carefully read the most ancient authors know very well that the Persians in former times—during their great and flourishing Monarchy or Empire, founded by the force and valor of Cyrus the Great, and continued thereafter for many long years in all perfection, excellence, and prosperity until the last of their Monarchs or Emperors named Darius, who was vanquished by Alexander the Great, King of Macedon—used the Chaldaic or Assyrian language <note>The author likely refers to Aramaic, which served as the *lingua franca* or administrative language of the Achaemenid Persian Empire</note>. This was like a natural, maternal, and ordinary tongue to them in their speech and writing, both common and familiar. Nevertheless, according to Herodotus in Book 3 of his *Histories* and the Book of Esther, chapters 1, 2, 3, and 8 in the Bible, they made use in their state affairs sometimes of their aforementioned language, sometimes of the Greek language, and sometimes of other foreign languages toward their subjects and tributaries, depending on how they understood and spoke said languages. This can be seen in several fine passages cited in the first book of *The Sovereignty of the Kingdom of the Persians* <note>original Latin: "Regio Persarum principatu"; a work by Barnabé Brisson published in 1590</note>. Furthermore, we find in ancient histories that Alexander the Great, having found the tomb of Cyrus, King of Persia, uncovered and ransacked, put to death the one who had done it. And having read the inscription which was in Persian letters and language, he ordered it to be written also in Greek letters and language underneath; the substance of the inscription being as follows:

> *O man, whoever you are, and from wherever you come: for I am certain that you will come: I am Cyrus, he who conquered the Empire for the Persians; I pray you, do not envy me this small bit of earth that covers my poor body.*

For he, among other impious and horrifying dogmas, taught that it was lawful and consistent with the laws of nature for a brother to be joined with his sister, a father with his daughter, a grandfather with his granddaughter, and what is most wicked (O laws! O nature!) for a son to be joined with his mother. Two lights of Roman poetry, clearly revealing these rituals, sang of them. Catullus wrote:

For this reason, Great Mother Earth herself, the nourisher of all, fleeing such foul and horrifying monsters, refused by any means to receive their corpses into her peaceful bosom (being spurred to vengeance by holy God). So that Zoroaster might veil this disgrace with a cloak of piety, he taught that the most holy rite of burial was not to be enclosed in the bowels of the earth, nor consumed by fire, but to be cast out in the fields to be dissolved by the air—by whose benefit you sustained your life for many years—or to be torn apart and consumed by birds, which you often nourished with your body while you lived.

Hence, all Persians would immediately carry out the body of the deceased and deport it outside the town, exposing it on the bare ground, naked, to be devoured by dogs and obscene birds. In this manner, once the flesh was consumed, the naked bones would rot, scattered across the fields. Furthermore, if birds did not immediately fly to a corpse, or if dogs did not run to tear it apart on the spot, they believed that man’s morals had been impure, his soul unjust and worthy of the abyss <note>original: "barathro," referring to a deep pit or hell</note>, and dedicated to an evil demon. 

Then, with the greatest grief, his friends would mourn him as one truly dead and not a participant in a better fate. However, they proclaimed him who was most quickly devoured to be most happy; they regarded his soul with great admiration as being most excellent, very similar to God, and destined to fly to the blessed seats. 

The common and more obscure crowd, if any among them in the army were afflicted by some sharp disease, were led out while still breathing and conscious. A piece of bread, a jar of water, and a staff were placed beside them, so that as long as they were able to use food, they would not be without it; and with the staff, they might ward off and drive away the attacking wild beasts and the feasting scavengers while they still had some strength. But if they had not yet died, yet the force of the disease had overcome them to the point that they could no longer move their hands, then the miserable wretches, half-dead and already beginning to give up the ghost, were most cruelly devoured, deprived of all sweetest hope of enjoying the breath of life. 

Many also, when they had recovered, returned home like characters in a play or tragedy, returning from the dark gates of the underworld, gaunt and pale, terrifying those they met. If anyone returned in such a state, everyone turned away from him and fled as if from a marked man, as one still dwelling among those below the earth. Nor were they permitted to resume their former way of life until the ritual pollution of their expected death had been expiated by the Magi, and their life...

A miraculous event also occurred to certain Philosophers returning from Persia to Rome (during the reign of Khosrow <note>Likely Khosrow I, the Sasanian king known as Anushirvan the Just (r. 531–579 AD).</note>, the most powerful King of the Persians) which revealed the same reason for this foul burial rite. For when they were resting in what was once Persian territory, they caught sight of the corpse of a dead man, neglected and cast aside unburied. Pitying the iniquity of that barbarian law, and deeming it in no way just to ignore nature being thus insulted, they had their servants cover the corpse as best they could and buried it, mounding the earth over it.

In the night that followed, while everyone was sleeping, one of them—by Hercules, I do not know which one, for I do not know his name—appeared to himself to see an old man. This man was not known to him, but was grave and venerable, displaying his devotion to Philosophy by both the style of his clothing and his long, flowing beard. He called out to him, as if exhorting and commanding:

> *Leave not the unburied and naked corpse in the tomb*
> *To be torn by dogs and serve as food for birds.*
> *For Mother Earth, who receives all, does not accept him*
> *Who dared to defile his mother with an unspeakable deed.*
> <note>original Latin: "Ne tumulis inhumatum ac nudum linque cadauer... Qui matrem est ausus facto vitiare nefando."</note>

Immediately awakened by fear, he reported his dream to the others; at first, they were uncertain what the dream might portend. However, when they rose at dawn and continued their intended journey, passing through that same field (as the terrain required) where they had provided the sudden burial, they found the corpse naked once more, lying atop the mound, as if the Earth, indignant and acting of her own accord, had vomited it back up in anger. Struck by the miracle of this sight, they continued their journey, performing no further final service for the man. Weighing the dream, they finally came to the conclusion that the Persians suffer this punishment and vengeance because of their shameful unions with their own mothers.

The successors of this Zoroaster embraced nearly these same dogmas: that the Gods should not be represented by any image, and that those who assign the distinction of sex to them sin most grievously. For this reason, Xerxes <note>The Persian King of Kings who invaded Greece in 480 BC.</note> burned all the temples of Greece, deeming it wicked for the Gods to be expressed in images or confined within the narrowness of walls. They asserted that the air swarms with demons who instill themselves into our eyes like miasmas <note>Polluting vapors or contagions.</note>. They wore white clothing; the ground was their bed; their food was vegetables, bread, and cheese, which they would place into their mouths fixed upon the tip of a reed staff. 

They were possessed by a supreme devotion to divination and excelled greatly in it. Thus, when the Parthian throne was vacant and the queen was pregnant—though she was still in the early months of conception—the leading men of the empire ordered them to declare whether the Queen was carrying a male or a female. First, so that their response might be more certain, they brought in a mare near to foaling and pronounced correctly upon its offspring; then they asserted the Queen was carrying a male child. The Princes of the empire, placing faith in this statement, placed the royal tiara <note>cidaris: a high, stiff Persian headdress or diadem.</note> upon the Queen's womb, proclaiming the embryo as King and distinguishing him with a noble name. Thus Shapur <note>Sapores: Shapur II (r. 309–379 AD), the only king in history to be crowned in utero.</note> was born after a few months with his Kingdom, and in it he both grew up and grew old, his life being extended to seventy years.

Liutprand of Cremona <note>A 10th-century historian and Bishop of Cremona.</note> calls them the Pizenaci, and Regino <note>Regino of Prüm (d. 915), a Benedictine abbot and chronicler.</note> calls them Pezinati—perhaps by a clerical error, which is easily committed by writers when dealing with names they do not understand. There is the same inconsistency regarding this name even in the Greek manuscripts. The Suda <note>A massive 10th-century Byzantine encyclopedia, formerly attributed to an author named Suidas.</note> also testifies that in his time they bore the name of the Patzinacitæ [Pechenegs], and certain of them were called Gruthungi and Dagci, who are European Scythians; Chalcocondylas <note>Laonikos Chalkokondyles (c. 1430–1470), a Byzantine Greek historian.</note> identifies them as those Sachatei.

The Albani are from the race of Scythians who are called Hamaxobii [wagon-dwellers], says Evagrius Scholasticus <note>A 6th-century Syrian scholar and historian of the Christian church.</note>. Nicephorus Callistus also mentions these. Today, however, as Herberstein <note>Siegmund von Herberstein (1486–1566), a diplomat and author of the first major European work on Russia.</note> attests, they are called **Tartars** by foreigners, but they themselves name them *Berfermani* or *Befermani*. Niger <note>Dominicus Marius Niger, a 15th-century Venetian geographer.</note> claims they call themselves *Matius* in their own language. According to Thevet <note>André Thevet (1516–1590), a French explorer and writer.</note>, they are called *Ator Albacaran* by the Arabs. These are the nations of the Scythians in Herodotus: the Anchatae, Arpoxae, Catiari, Traspies, and Paralatae; he adds that the name for all of them is the **Scoloti** <term>skolótēs</term> <note>original: <term>σκολότης</term></note>.

A great many are enumerated by Pliny, such as the Alani, Amordi, Apellae, Aorsi, Antariani, and Arimaspi (who were previously the Calcidiri), the Ariacae, Aroteres, Asaei, Camae, Camacae, Cotieri, Daci, Dahae, Edones, Essedones, Euchalae, Histi, Getae, Hamaxobii, Massagetae, Napaei, Octei, Pesici, Roxolani, Rhymnigi, Sacae, Sarmatians, and Satarchi. In Ptolemy, we read of the Grimaei, Abii, Agathyrsi, Azami, Aorsi, Ariacae, Anarei, Ascatancae, Aspisii, Chetae, Charau, Corasphi, Cacassae, Galactophagi <note>literally "milk-eaters"</note>, Hippophagi <note>literally "horse-eaters"</note>, Iastae, Iordii, Iotae, Iaxartae, Massae, Mologeni, Machageni, Norossi, Nomastae, Orosbes, Orgasi, Rhobasci, Sanitae, Sasones, Suebi, Susobeni, Setiani, Thaces, Taupuraei, Tabeini, Tybiacae, and Zaretae. Trebellius Pollio, in his *Life of the Emperor Claudius*, also includes these peoples of Scythia: the Peucini, Trutungi, Austrogoths, Virtingui, and Sigipedes.

In the lexicon of Stephanus [of Byzantium] *On Cities*, we read of these: the Aspilas (these are peoples of Colchis in the *Circumnavigation* <note>The *Periplus* of the Euxine Sea, a maritime guidebook by Arrian.</note> by Arrian), the Budini, Daias, Dassas, Heiuros, Euergetas, Edos, Iamas, Iamos, Bechir, Iseros, Lazos (of Colchis, according to Arrian), Matycetas, Maeotas, Myrgetas, Parthyacos, Sanigas (<term>sanígai</term> <note>original: <term>σανίγαι</term></note>, also of Colchis near Sebastopolis, according to Arrian), and Tyrmemenios. Mela <note>Pomponius Mela, a 1st-century Roman geographer.</note> places some of them as Nomads. Likewise, the Suda says they are also called *Hamaxophorei* [wagon-carriers]. Pliny complains, in describing them, of the inconsistency of authors because of—as he adds—the innumerable tribes, so much so that their name (as he says in another place) passes everywhere into the Sarmatians and Germans. Strabo writes in Book 1 that all known regions toward the North were previously called by one name: either Scythians or, as in Homer, Nomads. Likewise in Book 2, he reports that the ancient Greek writers applied the name of Scythians and Celto-Scythians to all the Northern nations; Ptolemy agrees with this opinion in his *Tetrabiblos* [Four Books]. Those older than these divided them such that all who lived above the Euxine [Black Sea], the Ister [Danube], and the Adria were called Hyperboreans, Sauromatae, and Arimaspi, while those beyond the Hyrcanian [Caspian] Sea were called Sacae and Massagetae. Philostratus encompasses the Scythians within the Ister, Tanais [Don], and Thermodon rivers. Trogus bounds them by the Pontus [Black Sea], the Riphaean mountains, Asia, and the Phasis river. Read of the Scythian customs in Theophrastus <note>Likely referring to the Hippocratic work *On Airs, Waters, and Places*, which discusses Scythian biology and culture.</note> on air and waters.

LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE. 515

The region which the Scythians now inhabit is said to have once belonged to the Cimmerians, says Herodotus in *Thalia* <note>The third book of Herodotus's *Histories*.</note>. I believe he speaks of the European Scythians. Julius Pollux (in Book 8, *On the Athenian Markets*) noted that the Scythian Archers were called <term>toxotai</term> <note>Greek: "archers".</note>. Even to this day, we interpret the name of the people of the Scandinavian peninsula—among whom are the Celto-Scythians—as "archers." See Scythia Minor, Pontica, Thracensis, and the Scytho-Germans under the entry for *Molsia*.

In Ptolemy, Scythia is twofold; both parts are in Asia, separated by Mount Imaus <note>A name used by ancient geographers for the central Asian mountain ranges, including the Himalayas, Pamirs, and Hindu Kush.</note>. Thus, they are designated as "within" and "outside" the Imaus. Villanomanus <note>Michael Servetus, who edited Ptolemy’s *Geography* under the name Villanovanus.</note> writes in his edition of Ptolemy that the Kingdom of Cathay [China] contains these Scythias. That which is within the Imaus seems to me to occupy a great part of Tartary. That which is situated outside the Imaus is called "Mongal" by the Barbarians and "Ancient Tartary" by more recent writers, according to Marius Niger. Arias Montanus, in his *Biblical Appendix*, believes that Scythia within the Imaus is the land the Hebrews call "Dicla."

Besides these, there is another Scythia in Europe (which Ptolemy calls Sarmatia) found in Herodotus, Pomponius Mela, and other ancient historians. Unless I am mistaken, this is the region Jordanes <note>A 6th-century historian of the Goths.</note> refers to, which he writes the Goths called *Ouim* in their own language; Conrad of Lichtenau reads this as *Ocimnin* from the same author. Strabo calls "Little Scythia" that region located between the Borysthenes [Dnieper River] and the Tauric Chersonese [Crimea]. According to Usuard (for November 3rd), Scythia is also the name of a certain metropolitan city in Phrygia. See also *Indoscythia*.

Ptolemy describes Indoscythia as a region of India stretching along the Indus River; Arrian, in his *Periplus*, names the same region simply "Scythia." The "Southern Scythians" <term>Notioi Skythai</term> <note>Greek: "Southern Scythians".</note> are mentioned by Dionysius Periegetes.

### On the Tartars.

It seemed very necessary to me to report in this chapter what the ancient Hebrew, Greek, and Latin authors left in writing regarding the ancient Scenites <note>From the Greek *skēnē* (tent); a term used by ancients for nomadic "tent-dwellers."</note> and Nomads, before entering into a discussion of the Tartars and their language. This is confirmed by the great Saint Augustine in the eighteenth book, seventeenth chapter of his *City of God*. Regarding this fourth chapter of Genesis, Rabbi Solomon [Rashi] and Rabbi Isaac write that Abel, son of Adam, was the first shepherd of sheep and other beasts <note>The author likely conflates Abel's role as a shepherd with the invention of nomadic infrastructure attributed to Jabal.</note>, having invented carts, tents, and pavilions in order to move and change countries, lands, and habitations often, for the convenience of grass and pastures. For this reason, he was called "the father of those who dwell in tents and pavilions," as confirmed by Gilbert Génébrard in the first book of his *Chronography*. Furthermore, the most inquisitive Rabbis assure us that after the Flood, almost all the children of Noah lived in tents and pavilions. The Hebrew word אהל <note>original: *Ohel*</note>, in this chapter, signifies a moving and unfixed tabernacle: a way of living in such tabernacles or tents that was maintained by the Patriarchs who came after the second age, as can be seen in several different places in the Holy Hebrew Scriptures; in *Polydore Vergil*, book 3, chapter 9, *On the Invention of Things*; and in the commentators of *Flavius Vegetius*, book 1, chapter 3, on military matters. This being presupposed, we shall say that the Scenites were anciently certain peoples of Arabia Felix <note>Literally "Happy Arabia," the fertile southern part of the Arabian Peninsula.</note> (just as there are still some today in this province toward the North called Arabs, according to the report of *Ludovico di Varthema* in his *itinerary*). They were named *Scenitæ* in ancient times by the Greeks <gloss>from the word for tents or pavilions</gloss>, in which they lived, as recorded by *Pliny* (book 5, chapter 11, and book 6, chapters 26 and 28 of his *Natural History*), following *Strabo* (books 1, 2, and 16 of his *Geography*). *Solinus* (chapter 36) and *Plutarch* (in the life of *Lucullus*) write that *Tigranes* <note>Tigranes the Great, King of Armenia (reigned 95–55 BCE).</note> forced a change in the way of life of these wandering people, who had no houses other than the tents or pavilions they always carried with them; this King made them settle near him to employ them in the business of trade. The Kurds <note>original: "Cuodes"</note> of today do the same in Assyria, according to the modern Syrian geographers, who note in their works that in the southern part of Mesopotamia there are currently Arabs formerly called *Scenites*. These remain shepherds to this day who rarely stop in one place, but rather change lands and countries according to where they find grass to feed their beasts and flocks.

As for the Nomads, *Herodotus* in several places in his works; *Strabo* (books 16, 7, 10, and 11 of his *Geography*); *Pausanias* in his *Attics*; *Justin* (book 2); *Pomponius Mela* (book 2, chapter 1, and book 3, chapter 5); *Pliny* (book 4, chapters 12, 13, and 17, and book 5, chapter 3); *Sallust* in the *Jugurthine War*; *Solinus* (chapter 29); *Hippocrates* in his *treatise on Air and Waters*; and *Athenaeus* (book 11, chapter 1 of his *Deipnosophistae* <note>A Greek work title meaning "The Banquet of the Learned."</note>) all make ample mention of these peoples. Modern cosmographers hold that the Numidians in Africa currently live in this same manner. Some report that *Homer* had knowledge of these peoples, whom he calls *Ἐνετούς* <note>The Eneti or Heneti, a tribe mentioned in the Iliad.</note>, and whom he places and locates in Paphlagonia. At present, there are several kinds of these nomadic and wandering shepherds in many parts of the earth, such as in our Europe, principally in the Northern countries, named Sargaces and Osyles. In Asia, those who live toward the Caspian Sea were anciently called Parni and Daces; in Africa, those who inhabit the Ammonic region. Modern geographers tell us the Nomads were a people of Africa located in the region of Zeugitana and Mauritania who were eventually called Numidians, according to *Festus Pompeius*. All of them issued and descended from the Persians, and were thus called Nomads <gloss>from the Greek word meaning 'to graze'</gloss>, because they devoted themselves entirely to pasturage, as reported by ancient Greek authors and *Henri Estienne* in his great *Treasury of the Greek Language* under the Greek word <term>nemo</term> <note>original: *νέμω, -εις*; meaning "to pasture" or "to distribute."</note>. Modern authors call them Zuphones. To tell the truth, the Scythian Sarmatians or Sauromatians were the true Nomads and <term>Hamaxobites</term> <note>From the Greek meaning "wagon-dwellers."</note> of the ancients, who have been succeeded by the Tartars of today, living in the same sort and manner. This is confirmed by a certain Arab geographer named *Abulfeda Ismail*, in one of his Geographies, placing the Goths and Magogs beyond the northern borders of Tartary. This is repeated by André Thevet in his Geographical Maps, and François de Belleforest in Book 4, Chapter 5, Volume 2 of his *Geography*, and Book 2, Chapter 10 of his *Universal History*. Regarding the Scythians and Scythias of the ancients, so named after Scythes, son of Shem and Araxa, we must presuppose that it is very certain—according to the accounts of modern geographers and cosmographers—that there are two Scythias, or Sarmatias, divided and partitioned by the river Tanais <note>The River Don in modern-day Russia.</note>: one in Asia and the other in Europe. The Asiatic one is described thus: leaving aside what is on this side of the Tanais or Don toward our Europe, it is that great expanse of land which extends from the said Tanais toward the Caspian Sea, truly and properly called Asian Sarmatia; which, speaking generally of both the East and North, is of very great space and length. The majority of writers who have mentioned Sarmatia have only described the one in Europe; if they touched upon the Asiatic one, they only knew it under the name of the Scythians, since Scythia (now generally called Tartary) is of a marvelous extent, reaching from the Tanais to the easternmost sea, and comprising the northernmost parts on that side down to the Indies. Asiatic Sarmatia, currently called Sargatia or Cumania <note>The land of the Cumans, a nomadic Turkic people.</note> (although Cumania is properly a part of the Colchian country), has for its boundaries to the North <term>Septentrion</term> the unknown land, not yet fully penetrated by anyone, being beyond the Riphean Mountains <note>A legendary mountain range in Greek geography, once thought to be the source of the North Wind.</note> or the "girdle of the world" according to the ancients. To the West <term>Ponent</term> lies the Frozen Ocean and the other Sarmatia—namely, the European one—as far as the Tanais River <note>The Don River.</note> and where it flows into the Black Sea <note>original: "mer noire, ou maiour" (Black Sea or Greater Sea).</note> at the Maeotian marshes <note>The Sea of Azov.</note>. The coast of these marshes as far as the Cimmerian Bosporus is also part of this region. To the South, by a bend in the "Greater Sea" <note>The Black Sea.</note>, it is bounded as far as the place where the Corax River flows into that same sea, extending to the lands of the Colchians and Georgians, and as far as the Sea of Abachu, or Bacchu, or Caspian <note>The Caspian Sea, often named after the city of Baku.</note>, and to where the Erdil River—named Volga or Rhà—discharges into the sea. Toward the East is Scythia, along the aforementioned Volga River, until it turns back toward the West and ends its course in the unknown land. This is how Ptolemy described it in Book 5, Chapter 9, Table 2 of Asia. Adding to this description what Pliny (Book 6, Ch. 17), Pomponius Mela (Book 3), and Herodotus (Book 4) wrote of the northernmost lands unknown in Asia during their times, we learn—according to Giosafat Barbaro in the book of his voyage to Tana, Ambrogio Contarini in Chapter 7 of his voyage to Persia, Hayton the Armenian in his books on the Tartars, Maciej Miechowita <note>original: "M. Michou"</note> in Book 1 of *Asiatic Sarmatia*, Sigismund von Herberstein <note>original: "Sigismond Liber"</note> in his *Commentaries on Muscovy*, Olaus Magnus and Johannes, Bishops of Uppsala in Gothia, in their *Northern Histories*, Paolo Giovio in Book 14 of his *Histories*, and André Thevet in Book 12, Chapter 9 of his *Universal Cosmography*—that these lands are today populated and inhabited by various sorts of people and nations. Those furthest North in Sarmatia do not labor or sow their lands; they have no bread, wine, or ale <term>ceruoise</term>, but live miserably. Keeping to the woods and the grottoes of the earth, they sustain themselves on fish and the meat of wild beasts, of which they have an abundance, quenching their thirst with beautiful pure water and being clothed in the skins of wild animals. And it is quite certain (even though Pomponius Mela in Book 3 and Solinus in Chapter 26 write of these regions that they are very temperate and filled with a pleasant sweetness of air in the depths of the North) that it is a pure fable to say these regions are temperate. For it is certain there is no misery compared to that of those who inhabit them, because they have no bread, wine, nor anything that a man might desire for his life; they are incessantly attacked by the rigors of winter and the harshness of extreme cold. At the winter solstice they have perpetual night, and at the summer solstice continual day—and even then with a very sluggish heat, without strength, because the Sun at that time only casts its rays upon them obliquely and sideways. Nor does one see in these countries—as some ancient and modern authors have believed—men with only one eye, nor those said to have two heads; nor are any such found.

And without lying, it is a great matter that from these parts of the North, according to the saying of the Prophet **Jeremiah**, it never happened that iniquity and misfortune did not spread over the earth, as **Jordanes** <note>A 6th-century Byzantine historian of Gothic origin</note> verifies in his book on **Gothic matters**. And the more Northern these peoples are, the more horrible and enraged they are in their face and gaze, both by nature, which makes them thus hideous, and by themselves, who artificially fashion themselves into such fury and deformity: nevertheless, the coarse air that strikes those furthest North makes them fat, heavy, and pot-bellied, because their humors cannot evaporate, the air containing them inside and thus making them bloated: And in fact, just as the Scythians neighboring **India** are of quite beautiful stature, gay, nimble, and cheerful, one also sees those who belong to the aforementioned Hordes to be swollen, heavy, small, flat-nosed, and bristly, having short legs and other such imperfections;

# HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF THE...

...as was explained previously. In addition to the Hordes mentioned above, there is that of **Colmack** <note>The Kalmyks, a Mongolic people of Central Asia</note>, who are among the most Northern; they honor and worship the Sun, or else they have a piece of red cloth which they hang from the end of a pole, and to this they show reverence, bowing their knees before it and worshiping it, praying to it in their times of need. The **Tartars** <note>A historical term used by Europeans to describe various Mongolic and Turkic nomadic peoples</note> who are further away, and who are closest to the **Northern Sea** <note>The Arctic Ocean</note>, are all either Idolaters, or without any knowledge or opinion of any divinity. I say that they have not forgotten their ancient follies, especially in the country of **Tarsent**, which is the true **Tartary** beyond **Turkestan**. The Tartars living there, named **Kirgesses** <note>The Kyrgyz people</note>, live like the others in hordes, gathering in great multitudes. When they are within a wood or in open country where there are trees, the one performing the office of Priest among them takes blood, milk, and dung from their herds and horse-studs, and mixes it with earth in a vessel. Then, climbing a tree, he delivers to them I know not what sermon on their foolish opinions; when it is finished, he scatters this liquid over the people in the manner of holy water. The abominable abuse of these **Kirgesses** is that they take and receive this fine sprinkling as their God, and worship or recognize no other, so that their God is foul, ephemeral, and dependent on the will of the one who distributes it to them. 

Furthermore, although the **Turks** are descended from these Tartars, as we have demonstrated before, they are nevertheless different from one another in several things, specifically in that they have different religions: for although the Tartars admit the law of **Mahomet** <note>original: "Mahomet" — the Prophet Muhammad</note>, they mix it with Idolatry; moreover, the Turks are quite civil and friendly to everyone, while on the contrary, the Tartars are fierce and savage. Their clothing is also different, even their headwear: the Turks wear **Turbans**, and the Tartars pointed caps, around which there is a white band, very well furred, along with the rest of their garments. 

In matters of war, there is likewise a great difference, as the Turks are good infantrymen <note>Soldiers who fight on foot</note>, and the Tartars are not, being able to do nothing unless they are on horseback. Besides this, the Turks have retained the use of the bow, which was formerly, and is still now, familiar to their brothers the **Scythians** <note>Ancient nomadic people of the Eurasian steppes</note>; for as for arquebuses <note>An early type of portable long gun</note> and pistols, they do not know what they are. As for the Prophet **Mahomet**, the Tartars hold him in some account for lack of any other religious practice; however, they mock him and his Prophets, just as the black **Moors** of Africa do for the most part. Furthermore, they despise the general resurrection and many other things which are observed and believed both in our Religion and in the **Mahometan** <note>Islamic</note> superstition.

This is the reason why in the morning you will see a Tartar—I mean even the greatest among them—who will go to gather some herbs or small fruits in the fields for his life [sustenance], such pasture...

->*On Africa, the third part of the world.*<-

Abraham Ortelius <note>A famous Flemish cartographer and geographer, creator of the first modern atlas.</note> in his *Synonyms* and *Geographical Treasury* writes what follows regarding this third part of the world.
<margin>Africa <term>Αφρικη</term></margin>
Africa, which is called Libya by the Greeks and Africa by the Latins, is called Chamesia in the Sacred Scriptures <note>original: "Chameſia"; likely a reference to the Land of Ham, son of Noah.</note>. Josephus <note>A 1st-century Romano-Jewish historian.</note> calls its people the Phutites. It is considered the third part of the world by the ancients. Joannes Leo <note>Also known as Leo Africanus, a famous traveler and diplomat of the 16th century.</note> writes that it is called Iphricia by the inhabitants. Thevet says that it is named Alkebulan <note>original: "Alkebulā"</note> by the Arabs and Ethiopians, and Besecath by the Indians. In our own tongue, it is generally called the Land of the Moors. In the works of Dioscorides, Serapio reads "Lyonsi" and "Linza," or likewise "Lintouin" for Africa.

There is also Africa Proper, which according to Ptolemy <note>An influential Greco-Roman mathematician and geographer.</note> is the part of Africa along the Mediterranean Sea, between the regions of Mauritania and Cyrene. It is called Zeugitana by Pliny, who divides it into Old and New Africa, as does Dion. It is the Naphthuhim to the Hebrews, according to the testimony of Arias Montanus <note>A Spanish orientalist and editor of the Antwerp Polyglot Bible.</note>. Today, the Kingdom of Tunis is located in this place. See Carthage, Libya, and Zeugitana.

Libya <term>Λιβύη</term> is a region which Stephanus <note>Stephanus of Byzantium, a 6th-century author of a geographical dictionary.</note> writes is also called:
*   Olympia <term>Ὀλυμπία</term> <gloss>meaning celestial or heavenly</gloss>
*   Oceania <term>Ωκεανία</term> <gloss>referring to the ocean</gloss>
*   Eschatia <term>Εσχατία</term> <gloss>meaning the remote or furthest land</gloss>
*   Coryphe <term>Κορυφή</term> <gloss>meaning the summit or peak</gloss>
*   Hesperia <term>Εσπερία</term> <gloss>the western land</gloss>
*   Ortygia <term>Ορτυγία</term> <gloss>land of the quail</gloss>
*   Ammonis <term>Αμμωνίς</term> <gloss>land of the god Ammon</gloss>
*   Ethiopia <term>Αιθιοπία</term> <gloss>land of the burnt-faced people</gloss>
*   Cyrene <term>Κυρήνη</term>
*   Ophiusa <term>Οφιούσα</term> <gloss>abounding in snakes</gloss>
*   Cephenia <term>Κηφηνία</term>
*   and Aeria <term>Αερία</term> <gloss>meaning airy or lofty</gloss>.

To the Hebrews, Libya is Ludim, as witnessed by Arias Montanus. In ancient inscriptions, Libya is more often read with a "y" in the first syllable. In the time of Procopius, that part of Africa which extends from Alexandria to the city of Cyrene was called Libya, as he himself testifies in the sixth book of *On Buildings*. In this stretch is also the Libya of Ptolemy, which he designates as "Proper" at the beginning of the fourth book of his *Geography*, where he numbers it among the eleven regions of Africa; however, in the description of it, he calls it the District of Libya. In Book 3, however, he mentions and makes only seven regions of Africa, a small difference...

**Leo [Africanus]** <note>original: "I. Leon"; referring to Joannes Leo Africanus, a 16th-century diplomat and author of the *Description of Africa*.</note>, cited above in the first book of his description of Africa, writes that the greater part of the Arabs who are in **Numidia** <note>A historical region in North Africa, primarily in modern-day Algeria and parts of Tunisia.</note> are versifiers who compose beautiful songs, in which they describe their battles along with the manner of hunting and the passions of love with such great grace and eloquence that it is a marvel; they make their compositions in verse and meter in the fashion of the vernacular poets of Italy, such as stanzas and sonnets. This same author, following what was said above, notes that the Arabs hold poetry in high regard and admire it greatly. Devoting themselves to it, they compose verses most often enriched with perfect elegance, even though their language is corrupted in many places; a poet, however little renowned he may be among them, is very welcome before their Lords, who, for the pleasure they receive from their verses, reward them generously. He assures you that it would be impossible for him to express the great grace they possess in their verses. These Arabs are those who presently inhabit the regions toward **Tunis** and **Tlemcen** <note>original: "Telesin"; a city in northwestern Algeria.</note>, who are in the pay of the Kings of those lands, and who go in summer to the frontiers to receive in the month of October from the treasurers of those Kings the pension given to them, after receiving which they retire to their deserts to pass the winter according to their ordinary custom.

A certain African, **Abdul Malik** <note>original: "Habdul Malich"</note>, a chronicler of the city of **Marrakesh** <note>original: "Maroc"</note> in Africa, has composed histories in his language divided into seven parts.

Beyond what we have reported above regarding the vernacular poets among the Arabs, there are also such poets among the Africans, and principally in the city of **Fez** in Africa, who compose verses on various subjects, and especially on love, expressing the passions they suffer for the thing they love; for their affections extend without shame to both sexes, as almost all **Muslims** <note>original: "Mahometistes." The author reflects a common early modern European bias in his description of local customs.</note> do regarding this sin every year on the day of the birth of their <note>original: "faux Prophete"</note> Prophet Muhammad. These poets assemble in the morning in the great square, where the Magistrates and principal men of their cities assist; there, these poets recite their compositions made in praise of the said Muhammad. He who is judged to have done best is praised and gifted by the judgment and sentence of the magistrates. In times past, the Kings had this trial held in their palace and gave to those who did best one hundred **ducats** <note>A gold coin used as a trade currency throughout Europe and the Mediterranean.</note>, a horse, a slave, and one of the most beautiful robes in his wardrobe; and each of the others received fifty ducats to encourage them to do well. But the Kings have forgotten this courtesy, though the Lords of the city of Fez still continue it.

## ON THE KABBALAH OF THE ARABS, TURKS,
## & Africans.

The book of the doctrine of the Prophet Muhammad <note>original: "Mahometh"</note>, received among the Muslims <note>original: "Mahometistes"</note> and followers of the Quran <note>original: "Alcoranistes"</note> as authentic, just as the Quran itself is, together with the Quranic doctors, create a certain Kabbalah <note>Here used to mean a mystical or numerological system of interpretation.</note> of numbers, entirely contrary to the true interpretation of them followed by the wisest in the Scriptures. For they say that the number 1 signifies that there is but one God, without having an equal, son, or companion; in this they show their foolishness, not seeing how much the threefold number <note>The Trinity.</note> is respected in Holy Scripture. The number 2 signifies Adam and Eve; 3 signifies Michael, Gabriel, and *Zaraphiel* <note>original: "Zaraphiel"; this name is unknown to the author, but likely refers to Israfil, the angel who blows the trumpet in Islamic tradition.</note>, a word unknown to us, whom they say are Archangels and Secretaries of the Divinity. By the number 4, they understand the Law of Moses <note>The Torah.</note>, the Psalms of David, the Gospel, and the *Al-Furqan* <note>original: "l’Alfurcam"; a name for the Quran meaning "The Criterion" or "The Distinction."</note>; and by 5, the prayers that God commanded Muhammad for himself and for his people; and 6 signifies the six days in which God made the world with its adornment. The number 7 includes the seven Heavens; 8 signifies the eight Angels who will have the charge of carrying the throne of God when He comes to perform the judgment; and 9 signifies the nine miracles of Moses. The number 10 signifies the ten days of fasting performed by those who go to Mecca—namely, three while going and seven after having completed their pilgrimage. By the number 11 are denoted the eleven stars that Joseph saw bowing down to him; 12 represents the twelve months of the year, but for 13, one must add to the aforementioned eleven stars the Sun and the Moon. By 14, they understand the fourteen luminaries that hang before the throne of God, each of which is one thousand five hundred years in length. By 15, they take the fifteenth day of the month of Ramadan—which they say is the month of March <note>The author incorrectly identifies Ramadan with March; as a lunar month, Ramadan rotates through the solar seasons.</note>—because on that day Muhammad received his Quran from Heaven. The number 16 represents the legions of Cherubim angels who are around the throne of God singing His praises. By 17, they say are understood the names of God which are between the summit of heaven and the deep abysses of the earth, without which—acting as obstacles—the world would be ruined by the heat that hell would vomit upon the earth. By 18, they understand the spaces that are between the air and the throne of God. The number 19 represents the arms of the river of Hell called *Saqar* <note>original: "Zaché"; likely referring to Saqar, one of the levels or names of hell in the Quran.</note>, which will cry out on the Day of Judgment, and to which the damned must respond. As for the number 20, its significance is that on such a number of days in the month of Ramadan, David received the revelation of the Psalms; and 21 because on such a day Solomon was born, just as on the 22nd of Ramadan God pardoned David for his sin regarding the murder of Uriah. They say that the 23rd is sacred to the Nativity of Jesus, son of Mary—which is false, for he was conceived in the month of March and the Virgin gave birth in December. They feign a change in their voice so it seems to be the Spirit giving the answer through their throat. > But those who have acquired, beyond their natural beauty, knowledge and experience of things, call these women *Sahacat* <note>original: *Sahacat*, an Arabic term for women who love women</note>, which is equivalent to what is called *Fricatrices* <note>original Latin: *Fricatrices*, literally "rubbers," a historical term for lesbians</note> in the Latin language. To tell the truth, they are afflicted by this wicked vice of using one another carnally; I cannot express it with a more proper term, nor one that suits them better. When they see a woman (among those who come to question them and seek advice on their affairs) who possesses any beauty, they fall in love with her just as a man would. In the name of the spirit, as reward and payment, they demand carnal copulation from her. Those to whom they make this immodest and dishonest demand—being unskilled in such deceptions—most often consent, thinking they are pleasing the demon. There are also many women who, having developed a taste for this game and being enticed by the sweet pleasure they receive from it, pretend to be ill. By this means, they send for one of these divineresses <note>original: *devineresses*, female fortune-tellers or seers</note>, and most often have the husband himself deliver the message. Then, they suddenly reveal their "illness" to them and where the remedy lies. To better cover their wickedness, they make the husband believe—foolish and simple as he is—that a spirit has entered his wife's body. Having her health as his priority, he is told he must give her leave to join the ranks of the divineresses and converse only in their company. They know how to perfectly and easily persuade some "John" <note>original: *Ian*, a period slang term for a simpleton or a cuckold</note>, who, consenting to it, prepares a sumptuous feast for this whole "venerable" band. At the end of the feast, they begin to dance to certain instruments played by the Black people. Then the woman has leave to go wherever she pleases. However, some men, subtly perceiving this trick, drive the spirit out of their wives' bodies with the terrible sound of dull thuds and a good thrashing. Others, pretending to the divineresses that they themselves are possessed by the spirit, deceive them by the same means the women used on their husbands.

The same Joannes Leo <note>referring to Leo Africanus, the 16th-century Moorish diplomat and author of *The Description of Africa*</note> in the book cited above, in the chapter on enchanters, writes the following words after what is stated above.

> There is yet another kind of diviner who are called *muhazzimin* <note>original: *muhazzimin*, likely referring to *mu'azzimin*, those who perform incantations or exorcisms</note>, which means enchanters. They are esteemed for having great power to deliver anyone who is possessed by the devil, for no other reason than that sometimes they emerge with their honor intact when the outcome follows what they requested. When this does not happen, they claim—to hide their ignorance and fraudulent deception—that the demon is an infidel <note>meaning a non-believer or non-Muslim spirit</note>, or else that it is some celestial spirit. Their manner of conjuring them is as follows: they form certain characters within circles in the middle of a hearth or other place; then they paint certain signs on the hand or forehead of the sick person. Having perfumed them with certain scents, they begin the enchantment, conjuring the spirit, asking it by what means it entered this body, where it is from, and what its name is, adding to this a command that it must leave immediately. There is yet another sort of enchanter who governs themselves by a rule called *Zairagia* <note>original: *Zairagia*, referring to the *Zairja*, a complex astrological device used by medieval Arab scholars to find answers to questions through numerical calculation</note>, that is to say, Cabala. But they do not study this science at all to gain knowledge of it, because they believe it is acquired naturally. And (to tell the truth) they give infallible responses to what is asked of them; but this rule is very difficult...

### Concerning the Region of the Ethiopians.

**A**braham Ortelius, in his *Synonyms* and *Geographical Treasury* <note>Abraham Ortelius (1527–1598) was a pioneering Flemish cartographer and the creator of the first modern atlas.</note> regarding Ethiopia <gloss>original Greek: Αἰθιόπια</gloss>, notes that Ptolemy identifies two regions of this name in Africa: one which he designates as lying below Egypt, and the other which he calls "Interior" [Inner] Ethiopia. This latter region is perhaps today's Zanzibar; whereas the former is now inhabited by the Abyssinians and is called "Abexim," or "Hhabas" by Garcia de Orta <note>Garcia de Orta was a 16th-century Portuguese physician and a pioneer of tropical medicine</note>, and—with the Arabic article added—"Alhabas" by Benjamin <note>Benjamin of Tudela, a 12th-century Jewish traveler</note>, the names differing only in the sound of the vowels. Pliny writes that all Ethiopia was formerly called "Etheria" and "Atalantia." These Ethiopians are called "Chusei" [Cushites] both by themselves and by all Asians, according to Josephus; Arias Montanus <note>Benito Arias Montano was a 16th-century Spanish orientalist and editor of the Antwerp Polyglot Bible</note> testifies to me that they are still called "Cushites" by the Cushitans today. Isaac Tzetzes records that they are called "Cepherides." Moreover, you will read that they were also called "Indians" under the entry for "Rhizophagi" [Root-eaters]. Ancient history, however, identifies both Eastern and Western Ethiopians, as Heliodorus names them in his 9th book: the former in Asia, the latter in Africa. Herodotus also places them in Asia among the Indians in his books *Thalia* and *Polymnia*, where the difference between the two groups is described. The *Chronicon* of Eusebius, at the year of the world 3580, has them rising near the Indus River, adding that they later settled around Egypt. Philostratus, in his 3rd book, writes—or perhaps trifles—that they once lived by the Ganges River before there was an African Ethiopia. But even the serious author Pausanias, in the 2nd book of his *Description of Greece*, places them near the Seres [Chinese] people and the island of Seria, where the custom of making silk from worms exists. Claudian, in his poem *On the Old Man of Verona* and in his *Panegyric on Stilicho*, calls these same Easterners "Black Indians." Likewise Tibullus in his 4th book, *In Praise of Sulpicia*. Pomponius Mela calls them the "Black Tribes." Strabo says the "Ethereal Ethiopians" are the furthest peoples within Carthage, reaching as far as the Cinnamon-bearing region. Herodotus, in his 3rd book, mentions the "Macrobians" [Long-lived] Ethiopians, who inhabit Africa toward the Southern Sea. An anonymous ancient commentator on Ptolemy’s *Quadripartitum* names a part of Ethiopia "Great Asia"; in Saint Jerome's *Life of Saint Matthias*, I read: "This is Ethiopia, where there is the incursion of the Apsari and the Port of Hyssus." Dorotheus calls this "Inner Ethiopia." However, in place of "Apsari," he puts "Phasis." Therefore, this Ethiopia—whether real or mythical—is located around Colchis <note>Colchis is an ancient region on the coast of the Black Sea, in modern-day Georgia</note>.

The Memnones <gloss>original Greek: μέμνονες</gloss> were a people of Ethiopia below Egypt according to Ptolemy, Pliny, and Stephanus. If I am not mistaken, Sidonius Apollinaris, in his poem to the elder Valerian, calls them "Memnonian Indians," saying they are scorched by the neighborly face of Aurora <note>Aurora is the Roman goddess of the Dawn; the text suggests they are darkened by being so close to the rising sun</note>.

The Rhizophagi <gloss>original Greek: Ριζόφαγοι, "Root-eaters"</gloss> are a people of Ethiopia dwelling along the Astaboras and Astapas rivers according to Diodorus Siculus. They are also called the Elei <gloss>original Greek: ἔλειοι, "Marsh-dwellers"</gloss> by Strabo in book 16. These Rhizophagi are placed among the Indians near the Estabaras River (as Pierre Gilles translates it) by Aelian in book 17 of *On Animals*; in Conrad Gessner’s printed Greek manuscript, the term "exa-imeni" <gloss>original Greek: ἐξαίμενοι</gloss> is used, but it is clear from Pliny, Mela, Strabo, and Ptolemy that it should read "Astaboras" <gloss>original Greek: ἀσταβόρας</gloss>, as they also describe these Root-eaters near this Astaboras, which is a branch of the Nile. From this passage in Aelian (and others, such as book 16, chapter 33, where he says Libya is near the Indians), it is understood that the Ethiopians living by the Nile were also called "Indians"; and that Virgil, in book 4 of the *Georgics*, was not without ancient authority when he also called these people "Indians" (though "colored" [sun-darkened] to distinguish them from others). Procopius agrees with this in his *On Buildings*.

...where he says the Nile flows out from the mountains of the Indians. Therefore, he calls Ethiopia "India." Hyginus also describes "Thebes of the Hundred Gates" <note>original: "Thebas Hecatompylas"</note> as being in India, and in Book 1 of his *Limits*, he writes that the Indians dwell from Egypt all the way to the Ocean toward the Equator.

We find in the records of the Greeks that the Egyptian land was named by them at various times *Melambolos* <note>original: μελάμβωλος, "black-soiled"</note>, *Hephaistia* <note>original: ἡφωισία, "land of Vulcan"</note>, *Potamia* <note>original: ποταμία, "river-land"</note>, *Ogygia* <note>original: ὠγυγία, "ancient"</note>, and *Aetia* <note>original: αἰθιοπία ὑπό αἴθυμα, perhaps meaning "Ethiopia under the burning heat"</note>. Cephidas, according to Tzetzes—or Pliny in Book 5, chapter 8, and Book 6, chapters 29 and 30 of his *Natural History*, and Solinus in his *Polyhistor*, chapter 33—reports that it was formerly called *Etheria*. However, according to Strabo in Book 2, there was only one part of it that bore this name, which was the final part toward Libya and the region called Cinnamon. 

This country was first named *Atlanie*, after the giant Atlas <note>Atlas was a Titan in Greek mythology, often associated with the Atlas Mountains in Northwest Africa</note> who is said to have reigned in Africa; and that a son of Vulcan named Ethiops, arriving there, gave it his name, *Ethiopia*. Others say that this word "Ethiopia" comes from the Greek word *aitho* <note>original: αἴθω</note>, which signifies "burned," and *ops* <note>original: ὤψ</note>, "face," because the Ethiopian country is situated beneath the Burned or Torrid Zone. Some others hold that this country took its name neither from the Greek words above, nor from Ethiops the son of Vulcan, but from a certain Oriental nation called the *Ethopeans*, which formerly lived along the Indus River. 

Beyond what is said above, I will report that the Ethiopians were formerly called *Auases* by the Egyptians, according to Strabo in Book 2, due to the diversity of colors of the earth in their country, and that the people themselves were distinguished by this variety; because of this, the name has remained with them even now. There is a region called *Gazacie*, named *Abas*, *Hhabas*, and *Alhabas* by good ancient authors (as seen in Girava's *Geography*), the Arabic article "Al" being added as a graceful ornament. From this comes the name *Abassia* <note>Abyssinia</note>, by which the Ethiopians of today are called "Abyssinians" by all the nations of the earth, and are known and understood by this word throughout the East, according to the report of Marco Polo in Book 3, chapter 43 of his travels. 

Strictly speaking, however, the true Abyssinians are those who inhabit Africa toward the North, bordering the deserts that separate Egypt from Ethiopia. They have their faces marked with a hot and glowing iron according to the custom of the country, which has caused many to believe they used this brand in place of Baptism—a thing which is entirely far from their intention. Those of this nation are also named *Nubians*, from the Province of Nubia, which at present is somewhat under the subjection and principality of the great Emperor or Christian King Prester John <note>Prester John was a legendary medieval Christian monarch whose kingdom was long sought by Europeans in Asia and later Africa</note>, of whom we shall speak at length hereafter. 

The Hebrews have written that *Chus* <note>Cush</note>—a Hebrew word—signifies in French "Ethiopian" or "black." This was the name of one of the sons of Ham, son of Noah, from which Chus the Ethiopians have descended and proceeded, named in the Hebrew language *Cushim* <note>original: כּוּשׁים</note>, as confirmed by Josephus in Book 1, chapter 12 of the *Antiquities of the Jews*, Eusebius in Book 9, chapter 4 of his *Preparation*, and St. Augustine in Book 16, chapter 11 of his *City of God*. In fact, these Hebrews call Ethiopia *Chus* in their language, the Portuguese call it *Cussia*, the Greeks *Aithiopia* <note>original: Αἰθιοπίαν</note>, and the Latins *India*. As the interpreter of Hebrew, Chaldean, and Greek names from the Old and New Testament says: "Ethiopia is called *Chus* in Hebrew, and is interpreted as black or blackness; for *Aithiopia* in Greek signifies heat or fire. The region of the Ethiopians, rising from the Indus river near Egypt..."

In this regard, a certain modern figure named Ludovicus Carretus <note>original: "Louys Carrectus"</note>—a Jew by nation and religion who later became a Christian—writes in his epistle to the Jews that the greatest part of the Nubians (so named after a city in their country which is currently bordered on the West by the country of Garga, one of its ancient dependencies, separated by deserts) are of the race of the Israelites. This country extends along the Nile, joining to the South the deserts of Goran toward the region of Amazen; to the North it has the land of Egypt and Barca; and to the East are the Nile and the Ethiopian lands, where the Nile is so low and muddy that it is impossible to find passage to go into Egypt. He claims the greater part of these Ethiopians are descended from the Israelites who were sent from Jerusalem to Ethiopia by Solomon, King of Israel, to the Queen of Sheba at her request, numbering twelve thousand people—namely, one thousand from each tribe of Israel. These Israelites multiplied like the sand of the sea, and each of them followed their own military signs and standards, as is more fully described in the *History of the Kings of Ethiopia* and in the travels to Ethiopia by Don Francisco Álvares, chapters 134, 137, and 138.

### *On the black color of the complexion of the Ethiopians, Negroes, Black people, or Moors of Africa.*

Some ancient Greek and Latin authors have written that the black color of the complexion of the Ethiopians was made and caused by the vehemence and insupportable heat and burning of the sun's rays, which struck directly upon their region located in Africa under the Torrid Zone. However, Herodotus in his third book and Strabo in the 15th book of his *Geography* have denied this for several reasons, attributing it entirely to the seed of their fathers—who were black and curly-haired by nature—who fathered them.

The children of *Cush* <note>original: "Chus"</note>, the first of his sons—who are the Ethiopians—were also born of a very black color, not because of their Province or Region being situated under the violent heat of the Sun’s rays (as most of the ancient Greek and Latin authors have written), but rather because of their origin. This is evidenced by the fact that under the Equator and the Torrid Zone, and in places closest to both tropics among the very black peoples who inhabit them today, there are found several others who are white or chestnut in color. These people are descended from the blood of *Abraham*, *Solomon*, and other Jews, whose ancestors came to live among these Negro or black peoples. Likewise, those who live in *India* under the same climate, or even the same parallel, would be of the same and similar color as the others mentioned above if they did not proceed from a different origin. Furthermore, in the *West Indies*, the Indians are for the most part of an olive or "Indian" color—that is to say, a dark ashen color—except for a few who live in a single place not far from the others, for which reason they are held as enemies by their neighbors. In contrast, the true Ethiopian Negroes or blacks take great pleasure and glory in their black color. What is more, as far as the 35th degree of latitude in Africa beyond the Equator, the peoples there are very black in color, contrary to those who are on this side of the said Equator—among whom are the Spaniards, Sardinians, Syrians, Arabs, Babylonians, Chaldeans, Persians, Susians, Turks, Tartars, Gedrosians, and other peoples situated 35 degrees on this side of the Equator at a similar latitude—among whom no Ethiopian, Negro, or black peoples are currently found. This leads us to believe entirely the opinion of the aforementioned Hebrews, who have asserted that *Cush*, named above and descended from *Ham* (who was white in color like his brothers *Japheth* and *Shem*), fathered these Ethiopians, Negroes, and blacks as a perpetual testimony of the fault and guilt he committed against his own father; as is confirmed by *Gilbert Génébrard* in Book 1 of his *Chronography*, following *Berosus* <note>A Hellenistic-era Babylonian writer and astronomer</note> in Book 3 of his *Antiquities*.

From the law of this **Cush**, therefore, the Greeks derived the names of the **Ethiopians** and the **Mauretanines** or **Moors**.

**Jean Bodin**, on the contrary to the characters named above, wrote in chapter 5 of his *Method of History* <note>original: "methode de l'histoire"</note> that which follows: "Now it is enough for us that the center of the east and the west is placed in **America**, because that region is separated from the **Indies** and **Africa** by infinite distances. The **Equator**, however, is the middle of the North and South as far as the whole universe is concerned; but of this hemisphere which is on this side of the **Equator**, it is the 45th degree of latitude: so that whatever lies between there and the pole is assigned to the North; the rest to the South. And since the ancients, except for **Posidonius** and **Avicenna**, defined the habitations of men by the tropical and polar circles, thinking there was no place for health or habitation beyond them, this error must be snatched away. For it has been found by frequent voyages that the region of the **Equator** is most healthy; but under the **Tropics**, the regions burn with incredible heat, and indeed the reason is at hand. For the Sun rises higher at the **Equator**, and is moved much more swiftly because of the size of the circle than in the tropics; furthermore, **Alvaresius** <note>Francisco Álvares, a Portuguese missionary and explorer</note> writes that the waters there freeze with frost in the month of June, provided the South wind blows. To this is added a great force of rains, the incredible height of mountains, and an abundance of forests; finally, the color and face of the men is not at all black, but like that of olives. On the contrary, under the **Tropics** there are violent heats, no rains, no forests, and rare rivers; a perpetual plain of sands, except in **Arabia** the Blessed and certain places in **India**, because of the nature of the East and the mountainous region. Finally, the dark skin of the inhabitants, not only of the **Ethiopians** but also of the **Indians**, as **Ctesias** <note>A Greek physician and historian</note> long ago and our own men have discovered. For I can hardly be persuaded by what a certain learned man relates, that men become black from the curse of **Cush**; and long ago the opinion of **Herodotus** was mocked, who thought the seed of **Ethiopians** was black. For it would be necessary for **Ethiopians** born in **Scythia** <note>An ancient region in Central Eurasia</note> to be black, and **Scythians** born in **Ethiopia** to be white, since all peoples have long ago been mixed by the multitude and frequency of colonies. But we see that men, just like plants, gradually degenerate when the soil is changed. This is the same reason why fire and the sun, as **Aristotle** teaches, stain men with a dark color; furthermore, **Pliny** writes that lions in **Ethiopia** are black, which the poet **Oppianus** testifies to having seen in his book on hunting." This same author, always continuing his discourse, says at the end: "And since under the tropics and both Poles..."

<summary>This page juxtaposes a theological explanation for black skin (the "Curse of Cush") with Jean Bodin's early scientific argument that skin color is determined by climate and environment rather than lineage. Bodin rejects the biblical curse and Herodotus's theories, citing modern explorers to prove that the Equator is habitable and that "men, like plants," change according to the soil.</summary>

> "The highest extreme of cold and heat is found under the Equator, yet the climate there is the same as for those who are positioned at the 30th degree; for here and there, **White Ethiopians** <note>original: 'Leuco Æthiopes' — a term used by ancient geographers for light-skinned groups in Africa</note> are said to exist. Under the Tropics, they are black beyond measure; toward the north, by a contrary reasoning, they are of a dark color. Then, up to the 60th degree, they emerge as ruddy; from there to 45, they are white; after 30, they turn yellow; and when yellow bile is mixed with black bile, they become greenish, until they emerge as dark and finally completely black under the tropics. Therefore, what **Hippocrates** says—that men toward the North are deformed by paleness and thinness—would be absurd, unless we refer to the extreme northern regions; yet the ancients say those closer to us are robust and tall. This was confirmed to me when I was in doubt by **Gaspar Holfter**, a Swede from the capital city of **Stockholm**, born in the heart of **Gothia** <note>Götaland, a southern region of Sweden</note>, who has a completely red face and hair, and is clearly <term>red-nosed <note>original: 'φοινικόρυγχος' (phoinikorynchos)</note></term>, of average height without any skin defect, broad-shouldered, and with very grey-blue eyes, though with dull vision, for he suffers from a constant cataract <note>original: 'glaucomate'</note>. **Linguetus the Frenchman**, famous for his learning and travels throughout Europe, often told me the same: that beyond Gothia men are dark and waste away with thinness, but in Gothia itself and **Sweden** they are ruddy, though not to be compared in size to the **Germans**. This also greatly troubled **Galen**, because **Hippocrates** and **Aristotle** wrote that <gloss>everyone toward the north is red-haired and thin-haired</gloss> <note>original: 'πάντες πρὸς ἄρκτον πυρρότριχες, καὶ λεπτότριχες'</note>, as if all were yellow-haired; whereas most from the extreme North seemed <gloss>red-haired</gloss> <note>original: 'φοινικότριχες'</note>. For those whose hair is red in **Britain** and **Germany**, the inhabitants say (as I have learned from them) that they trace their origin to the **Danes** and **Norwegians** who occupied the neighboring regions, and they are more wary of them; many such people are also in **France**, especially in **Westria** or **Normandy**, which fell to the Danes; but the Germans and Britons are almost all yellow-haired, etc." **A. Theuet**, book 2, chapter 13; book 4, chapter 6; book 12, chapter 5 of his *Cosmography*. **F. de Belleforest**, volume 2, leaf 1936, of his *Cosmography* says these words.

**Marco Polo the Venetian**, book 3, chapter 28, has left in writing that the inhabitants of the Province of **Maabar** <note>The Coromandel Coast of India</note> make themselves blacker by artifice, and paint their gods black with sesame oil, and their demon white, and of a white color.

**F. Lopez de Gomara**, book 6, chapter 21 of his *General History of the West Indies*, tries to give a reason why the **West Indians** <note>Indigenous peoples of the Americas</note> are of a tawny <note>original: 'lionasse'</note> or olive color.
