### On the language of the Prussians and Pomeranians.

Laonikos Chalkokondyles <note>original: "Nicolas Chalcondyle"; a 15th-century Byzantine historian</note> in book 3 of his *History of the Turks* says: As for the Permians <note>A people of north-central Russia</note>, they are situated above the Sarmatians toward the North, whose neighbors they are, using the same language. And it is said that these are very ancient peoples, entirely devoted to hunting, in which they employ the better and greater part of their time. Sarmatia, which stretches toward the sea, finally joins the lands of Prussia, currently governed by religious knights <note>The Teutonic Knights</note> who wear long, all-white cloaks marked with a double black cross. It is held that they are German in their speech and way of life, having a separate Order, much like those of Spain and Rhodes <note>Referring to the Orders of Santiago or Calatrava, and the Knights Hospitaller</note>.

Some historians have held that Pomerania and Prussia are one and the same thing, as they once were, because there has hardly ever been a difference in manners, ways of doing things, nor language between them, and there is no notable mark by which these two peoples can be separated; thus, most often, they are taken for one another. For when it is a question of Dantzig <note>Gdańsk</note>, it is placed in Prussia, although in truth it is in Pomerania, because the true Prussia is that which is enclosed between the sea and the rivers Vistula, Drwęca <note>original: "Deruãce"</note>, Ossa, and Neman <note>original: "Nemene"</note>. The Poles are today Lords of all Prussia, except for that portion which is along the sea, where the cities of Königsberg <note>original: "Kuniſperg"</note> are situated—which is to say, "King's Mountain" <note>original: "Montreal"</note>, the work of a King of Bohemia—Löbenicht <note>original: "Loefcat"</note>, Insterburg <note>original: "Augerbourg"</note>, Landsberg, Fischhausen <note>original: "Bieſtat"</note>, and Rosenberg, which are under a separate Duke <note>The Duke of Prussia</note>. This Duke, nonetheless, acknowledges the whole and holds it in faith and homage to the Kings of Poland, following the convention made in the year 1525 between King Sigismund and Albert, Marquis of Brandenburg and Grand Master of Prussia. In truth, the Poles could not do without this land without great inconvenience, for it opens and closes the sea to them, inasmuch as the Vistula river, which divides Poland as if into two halves, passes through Kraków and the other best [cities]...

Thirdly, I add that in the mentioned Suetonius, I would prefer to read "Albanians" rather than "Alans"; for these are people of Asia neighboring the Parthians. The Alans, however, are associated with the Europeans. Tacitus confirms my opinion in the *Annals*, books 12, 13, and 15. I know Zonaras writes that the Alans were called Albanians by the ancients; let him see to that. See "Scythians" and "Massagetae."

Whether the Finns <note>original: "Fenni"</note> should be ascribed to the Germans or the Sarmatians, Tacitus doubts. Althamerus thinks the *Phinnoi* [φίννοι]—whom Ptolemy places in this region—are Prussians or Lithuanians. But it seems to me, following Jordanes, they are those who today inhabit Finland. They are also in the Scandinavian peninsula, where there are also the *Scritifinni* <note>Literally "Skiing Finns," likely referring to the Sámi people</note> or *Christofinni*, but more towards the North. These are so named from a "barbarous" word for "leaping," says the Deacon <note>Paul the Deacon, an 8th-century historian</note>. I believe it comes from *schieiten* or *schryen*, purely Germanic words which signify to spring or to make large strides with legs apart while walking. For, according to the eyewitness Olaus <note>Olaus Magnus, a Swedish geographer</note>, they use wooden soles tied under the soles of their feet, with which they seem to glide through snow and ice with marvelous speed rather than run. The use of these is also among us in winter time. We call them *Serickschoenen* <note>An old Germanic term for skates or sliding shoes; literally "gliding shoes"</note>, as if one were to say "jumping shoes." We should see if they are the same as those called "Horse-feet" [Hippopodes] by ancient writers because of this swift running.

The Massagetae [μασσαγέται] are commonly called Alans [ἀλανοὶ], as Dion Cassius, Ammianus, and Gregoras write. Johannes Tzetzes says to consider the Massagetae as the Abasgians [ἀβασγοὶ]. Isacius Tzetzes writes that the Massagetae were later called Angi [ἀνγοὶ]. Evagrius and Procopius, in book 1 of the *Vandalic War*, call them Huns. Herodotus, whose description of them exists, places them to the East, across the river Araxes, in the region of the Issedones. According to Stephanus and Suidas, the Massagetae are around or within Arachosia. In Ptolemy, they are in Margiana and also in Sogdiana. To Laonicus, they seem to be the Chataidae. André Thevet <note>A 16th-century French explorer</note> calls them *Ahinadal*. Ptolemy has Massagetae in Margiana and others among the Sacae. See "Magog" and "Scythians."

### CHAP. LXIX.

Nicolas Chalcondyles, in book 3 of his *History of the Turks*, writes that the Lithuanians border the Poles, reaching as far as the Euxine Sea <note>The Black Sea</note> and the Sarmatians. Podolia—whose capital city is Leopoli <note>Lviv, in modern-day Ukraine</note>—extends from the Wallachians who live along the Danube to the Lithuanians and Sarmatians. And certainly, these people deserve some praise for this very reason: that they never wished to change their language but have always kept their own and still retain it, even though anciently they were divided into two parts, one of which had Princes and Lords whom they obeyed, and the other Chiefs and Captains to govern them. The Lithuanians, as far as their speech is concerned, share nothing with the Sarmatians, Hungarians, or Germans, nor with the Wallachians either; for they have a distinct language, and the capital city of the country is called

*Vilnius* <note>original: "Vilne"</note>, is large, rich, and well-populated. Thus one can easily recognize that this people is the most powerful in all those regions, and they yield in nothing of prowess and valor to any other whatsoever: for they fight every day with the *Prussians, Germans, Livonians, Muscovites, Tartars*, and other such races of people by whom they are surrounded, in defense of their frontiers and borders. In their customs and ways of doing things, in their clothing and manner of fighting, they nearly follow their neighbors, taking something from each. Now, this language of the *Sarmatians* of which we have spoken so much is the very same one used by the *Illyrians* or *Slavs* <note>original: "Eſclauons"</note> who live on the coast of the *Adriatic* sea quite near *Venice*: which language, called *Slavonic*, was anciently in very great use among all the nations of the *North* and the *East*, and throughout *Greece* as well. But as to being able to say which are the oldest, or who supplanted the others in their lands and dwellings: whether it was the *Slavs* who first passed into *Poland* and *Sarmatia* and settled there, or indeed the *Sarmatians*, having set out toward the *Danube*, conquered the land of *Mysia* and that of the *Triballi*, and *Slavonia* likewise, which extends, as said above, as far as the *Venetians*.

Sebastian Münster, in *Book 4 of his Universal Cosmography, in the chapter on the Province of Lithuania, a dependency of the kingdom of Poland*, holds that the *Lithuanians* use and speak the *Slavonic* or *Slavic* language as do the aforementioned *Poles*, because this language extends quite far and is the common tongue <note>original: "commune & vulgaire"</note> to many nations. The same author, in the subsequent chapter on certain cities of *Lithuania*, writes that these *Lithuanians* have four sorts of languages or dialects: the first is of the *Yotvingians* <note>original: "Lactzuuingiens"</note>, which is commonly called *Iauuinger*; the second is of the *Lithuanians* and *Samogitians* described above; the third of the *Prussians*; and the fourth is of the *Livonians*, inhabitants bordering the *Daugava* <note>original: "Dzuine"</note> River, which others call the *Dunk*. And although it is the same language among all of these, nevertheless one will not understand the other unless he has frequented all these lands. The ceremonies and customs of the *Latins* <note>Referring to the Roman Catholic Church</note> are kept in the said regions; but in the other neighboring ones, such as *Novgorod* <note>original: "Nouigrod, ou Neugarde"</note>, *Pskov* <note>original: "Pleſcouie"</note>, *Polotsk* <note>original: "Polocko"</note>, *Smolensk* <note>original: "Smoleuko"</note>, and in the parts of the *Russians*, they keep the ceremonies and customs of the *Greeks* <note>Referring to the Eastern Orthodox Church</note>.

Matthias of Miechów <note>original: "Matthias Michou"</note>, in *Book 2, Chapter 3 of European Sarmatia*, speaking of this matter, has said:

Northern historians affirm in their histories that a man named *Vytenis* <note>original: "Vuiteuné," a Grand Duke of Lithuania</note> was the first who began to bring these Lithuanians into view, and to give them fame and reputation among their neighbors, over whom in a short time they accomplished great things, with the help of the *Samogitians* who were then, and still are, one and the same people with them, and the *Yazygians* <note>original: "Iazinges," likely referring to the Sudovians/Yotvingians</note> who have since been entirely exterminated, so that the name barely remains. Nevertheless, their language is still used around the Castle of *Drohiczyn*. The Prussian tongue was also spoken there; but these Lithuanians have their own distinct and particular language, which is one with that of the aforementioned Samogitians, which the common people still keep: for the great lords have adapted to the *Polish* language, and even the preachers use it in their sermons for the instruction of the people, although it is not at all very well understood. *Sigismund von Herberstein* <note>original: "Sigismond Liber"</note> in Book 1 of his history of *Muscovy* confirms the above. Regarding the specifics of Lithuania, *Vilnius* <note>original: "Vilne"</note> is the capital city of the whole country, larger than *Kraków* <note>original: "Cracouie"</note>, the capital of Poland, but not so populated, nor the houses so crowded together: for they are all distinct and separated by squares and gardens. It is situated among hills and small mountains at the junction of the rivers *Neris* <note>original: "Vuelie"</note> and *Vilnia* <note>original: "Vilne"</note>, from which it takes its name. It is now surrounded by walls, having likewise several churches and monasteries of masonry, and among others that of the *Franciscans* <note>original: "Cordeliers"</note>, which is very magnificently built. However, there are more churches of the *Greek* or *Ruthenian* religion than of the Roman Catholic, even though the Episcopal seat is there. The next city today is *Trakai* <note>original: "Trochy"</note>, where there is usually a great number of Jews, who do not lend at interest but hold the tax farms and salt taxes <note>term: gabelles — a historical tax on salt and other commodities</note>. This Lithuania, bearing the title of Grand Duchy, was united and incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland by King *Władysław Jagiełło* <note>original: "Vuladislaus Iaghellon"</note> and his cousin *Vytautas Alexander* <note>original: "Vitoudus Alexandre"</note> at the assembly in the town of *Horodło* <note>original: "Rodlo"</note> on the River Bug on the 2nd day of October, 1413. It is governed like Poland by Palatins, Castellans, Chancellors, Captains, Marshal of the Land, and Marshal of the Court, and others.

## Of the Region of the Wallachians.

A. Ortelius in his *Geographical Synonyms* and *Geographical Treasury* states: Dacia <note>Greek: Dania</note> is a region of Europe according to Ptolemy. Strabo thinks the inhabitants were anciently called *Dacians* or *Davos* <note>Greek: Davous</note>, and he writes that they live toward the Danube near its sources. To this we may add what Philargyrus left written in his commentary on Book 2 of Virgil’s *Georgics*: "Certain people called the Dacians 'Daoi'," as Stephanus and Eustathius also say. The *Epitome* of Strabo says the same. Stephanus and Pliny note that those whom the Romans call Dacians, the Greeks call *Getae*. Regarding Dacia, Jordanes says: "This Gothia, which the ancestors called Dacia, is now called Gepidia." Suidas writes that the Dacians were called *Patzinacites* <note>The Pechenegs, a nomadic Turkic people</note> in his time.

Ancient Dacia, as Stephanus Broderithus teaches, today encompasses Transylvania, Wallachia, and Moldavia. It has various names: Mediterranean Dacia, Riparian Dacia <note>Dacia along the riverbanks</note>, Pannodacia, and Transylvania (or *Ultrasylvania*). Today, it is called *Weissenburg* <note>original: "Vuibenburghen"</note> by the Germans and *Erdély* <note>original: "Herdel"</note> by the Hungarians. Following the author Sabucus, the regions of Riparian and Mediterranean Dacia are mentioned by Eutropius, Aurelius Victor, Jordanes, Marcellinus Comes, and the *Book of Notitia*. The *Historia Miscella* places it between Dacia and Macedonia. Lazius places it between the rivers Tisza <note>original: "Tibiscũ"</note>, Maros <note>original: "Marisiũ"</note>, Körös <note>original: "Carisiũ"</note>, and the Danube. The same authors mention Mediterranean Dacia.

Today, as Lazius says, this land is inhabited by Transylvanians, Saxons, Hungarians, and the *Székelys* <note>original: "Cæculi"</note>, who are the descendants of the Hungarians. The same Lazius uses the term Alpine Dacia (though I know not on whose authority), which he interprets as Moldavia and Wallachia. Add to this the accounts of Leunclavius in his *Muslim Onomasticon*. The name *Pannodacia* is frequently used by Laonikos Chalkokondyles, who reports that it is named *Ardelium*. This Greek term is clearly fashioned from the common word *Herdel* <note>Erdély/Transylvania</note>. Moldavia is also called *Bogdania* by Laonikos. Godreccius writes that Transalpine Wallachia is called *Lesser Black Bogdania* <note>original: "Carabogdaná"</note> by the Turks, because it produces black grain. Laonikos also mentions *Black Bogdania*. Saint Paulinus describes a twofold Dacia in these verses on the return of Nicetas:

> And the Getae run
> And both Dacians:
> He who dwells in the middle lands,
> Or that well-cloaked neighbor
> Of the rich riverbank.
> <note>original Latin: "Et Getæ currunt / Et vterque Dacus / Quæ colit terris medio, / Vel ille diuitis multo / Bene pelleatus Accola ripæ."</note>

Sextus Aurelius Rufus attributes this division to Aurelian, naming them Moesia and Dardania. Eutropius says nearly the same. We have written more on this subject in the map of Dacia in our *Theatrum* <note>Referring to the *Theatrum Orbis Terrarum*, the first modern atlas</note>. Dacia is also a tract of Cappadocia, sacred to Jupiter, according to Strabo, Book 12.

Laonikos Chalkokondyles, Book 1 of his *History of Turkey*. A. Thevet, Book 20, Chapter 5 of his *Universal Cosmography*. B. de Vigenère in his *History of Poland*.

...to understand one another. How it happened that they, using almost the same speech, the same customs, and way of life as the Italians, came to take root in these borderlands, I have not yet understood, nor have I found anyone who could give a satisfactory account of it. Nevertheless, the common rumor is that they were people gathered from various places who first landed there without, however, doing anything worthy of memory or deserving of being included in this present history. Furthermore, one still sees today that they do not differ much from the Italians, as much in their ways of doing things as in their utensils, armor, equipment, and clothing, which are nearly the same for both peoples.

Sebastian Münster, in Book 4 of his *Universal Cosmography*, in the chapter on Wallachia—a part of Thrace formerly called Gethic <note>territory of the Getae, an ancient people of the Lower Danube</note>, which was partially subject in his time to the King of Hungary and the other to the Great Turk—writes that in this province, so-called because of the Flacci, who were descended from the Quirites <note>the ancient Roman citizenry</note> who came to inhabit it with a Roman colony: the Roman language <note>Latin</note>, though altered and corrupted in all sorts of ways so that it can hardly be understood by a Roman man, is current and in vogue there; a fact I have already noted above in the chapter on the language of the Hungarians.

The Histories of Poland state that the Palatines or Voivodes <term>Voivode: a Slavic title for a military governor or high-ranking commander</term> of Wallachia had at all times been tributaries to the Kings of Hungary, and under their protection and obedience, until after the death of King Louis around the year 1388. At that time, the affairs of the Hungarians being in total disarray, the Palatine Peter withdrew from them and came to Lviv <note>original: "Leopoly"</note> to swear an oath of fidelity to the King of Poland, Władysław Jagiełło <note>original: "Vuladislaus Iaghellon"</note>. This was afterward continued by his successors to the Kings of Poland. Regarding their origin and beginning, it must be understood that what was anciently called Dacia was a vast expanse of country bounded to the north by the river Dniester <note>original: "Nester"</note>, which separated it from Lower Russia and Podolia. To the west, it had the Jazyges Metanastae <note>an ancient nomadic tribe of the Pannonian Plain</note>; to the east, the Danube and Lower Moesia <note>original: "Mysie"</note>, later called Bulgaria; and to the south, the same Danube, which turns its course in this place toward Upper Moesia, which has taken the name of Bosnia and Serbia. Emperor Trajan, having finally subjugated it, transported Romans there to repopulate it and reduced it into the form of a province. But in the time of Gallienus, and later under Aurelian, the barbarians reconquered it. The Goths also threw themselves into it during the Empire of Gratian, such that the Wallachians are descended from this mixture. Having blended the customs, ways of doing things, and language of those mentioned above, they have created I-know-not-what apart, which no longer resembles any of them. Nevertheless, they also use Ruthenian <note>an old East Slavic language</note> and Slavic speech. Regarding their name, it is said that it was a Roman named Flaccus who first gave it to them, and from there they were called Falachi or Wallachi: for the letters F and V, being consonants, are easily exchanged for one another. Likewise, the Poles and all others who use the Slavic language call the peoples descended from the Italians by the common name of Wallachians <note>original: "Vualassiens"</note> or *Włosi* <note>original: "Vuloſſiés"; the modern Polish word for Italians</note>, which closely approaches that of Valaque. These people hold to the Christian Religion according to the usage and tradition of the Greeks <note>Eastern Orthodox Christianity</note>. And they have hardly been...

### *Concerning the region of the Livonians.*

Abraham Ortelius, in his *Geographical Synonyms* and *Geographical Treasury*, writes that in his *Life of Charlemagne*, Eginhard <note>the Frankish scholar and servant to Charlemagne</note> records a "Hilinonic War" undertaken by Charlemagne; Albert of Stade and Lichtenau read this as "Lilonic" <note>original: "Hilinonicum bellum... Eginaithus Lilonicum legit Alb. Stadensis"</note>. I believe these are corrupted terms and should be read as "Livonians" along with Aimoin, even if Krantz’s *Saxonia* reads "Liburnian" in this place <note>original: "Corruptas voces & Liuones legendum cum Aimonio puto... Liburnicum"</note>. But read what Reineck noted in the *Life of Charlemagne* published by him, who thinks the district of Lüne and the name Lüneburg take their name from these people.

### *Concerning the language of the Livonians.*

Sebastian Münster, in Book 3 of his *Universal Cosmography*, in the chapter on Livonia, writes these words concerning the language of these Livonians:

> This region is narrow, because of the Sea that presses it on one side and the neighboring peoples who hem it in—namely the Prussians, Russians, and Lithuanians. And although this province is not very large, there are nevertheless many languages of many nations contained within it; and the persistence of the diversity of these languages clearly shows that this entire nation was barbarian and uncivilized. Otherwise, if there had been any commonality of life among them, or any society of shared actions during war or peace, they would have adopted the same language and way of speaking, or at the very least there would not be such a great variety of languages among them. The situation is such that today there are four peoples among them who have nothing in common in their language with one another, namely the Livonians, Estonians, Letts <note>original: "Lertiens," referring to Latvians</note>, and Curonians <note>original: "Curons," people of the Courland peninsula</note>. The greatest Lord or Prince of all Russia without any doubt is the Muscovite, and the Grand Duke of Lithuania after him, then the King of Poland; other than these three, none claim anything there, and even the last two are now but a single Lordship. For Lithuania with its dependencies was united to the Kingdom of Poland by Jagiello <note>Jogaila, Grand Duke of Lithuania and later King of Poland</note>, son of Algirdas, around the year of Salvation 1386. Russia, therefore, according to its ancient description, takes its beginning at the Sarmatian mountains <note>The Carpathian Mountains</note> toward the source of the Vistula river. And from there it extends along the river Tyra, otherwise called the Dniester <note>original: "Nester"</note>, as far as the mouths of the Borysthenes <note>The Dnieper River</note>, which enters the Euxine Sea <note>The Black Sea</note>, quite near Moncastre <note>Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi</note>, which is now under the obedience of the Turk <note>The Ottoman Empire</note>. From there one must go upstream to Cherkasy <note>original: "Circassi"</note>, and then to Kyiv <note>original: "Chiouie"</note>, formerly the capital city of all Russia, where one crosses the water to traverse the Province of Severia <note>original: "Seuvere," a historical region in modern Ukraine/Russia</note>, and some other countries directly toward the Rising Sun <note>East</note>, until one reaches the springs of the Tanais <note>The Don River</note>, by which, according to the opinion of cosmographer nations, Europe is separated from Asia. They claim that from her, the first Christian among all the *Russians*, they have ever since kept the traditions of the Greek Church. By this means, the Emperors of *Constantinople*, *Basil* and *Constantine Porphyrogenitus* <note>Basil II and Constantine VIII</note>, gave him their sister *Anna* in marriage, in the year of Grace 983. At this place, he first preached the Christian religion and erected crosses and other holy items for prayer and the service of God.

> » <note>The text continues a quote from Matthias of Miechów</note> ...The Metropolitan is of Kyiv, which was formerly the Metropolis of Russia: he has subject to him Vladikas <note>original: "Vladicas", a term for Eastern Orthodox bishops</note> and Bishops of the Greek rite in Moldova and Wallachia as far as the river Ister, or Danube; one in Russian Chełm, another in the domain of the Lithuanians at Vladimir or Brest, a third at Pinsk or Mozyr <note>original: "Pinsenseu Murouusci"</note>, a fourth at Płock, a fifth at Lutsk, a sixth at Smolensk, and everywhere all other Vladikas and Bishops in the lands of the Muscovites, and extending into the North under the jurisdiction of the Muscovites. Isidore, formerly the Metropolitan of Kyiv, a Greek most skilled in language and learning, went with a hundred horses to the Council of Florence in the time of Pope Eugene IV, and returned to Russia with the teachings of the union with the Roman Church; the Muscovites, because he preached obedience to Rome, despoiled him and drove him to the brink of death. The Ruthenians <note>A historical term for the East Slavic inhabitants of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, including modern-day Ukrainians and Belarusians</note> follow the doctors and theologians of the Greeks, especially Basil the Great, Gregory Nazianzen, and John Chrysostom. They call Gregory Nazianzen *Bogoslou* in their own language, which in Latin sounds like "praising God" <note>original: "Bogoslou", meaning "Theologian"</note>. They also accept our Saint Gregory, the Roman Pope, especially his books of morals, which they read in translation; they call him in their language *Byessednic*, which means a speaker, persuader, or preacher <note>original: "Byessednic", from the Slavic 'besednik', meaning one who talks or discourses</note>. In the churches of the Ruthenians, they celebrate, read, and sing the divine services in the language of the Serbs, which is Slavonic. However, Christians of the Roman rite sing, pray, and read in the Latin language. In the churches of the Armenians, they use the Armenian tongue; in the synagogues of the Jews, they pray in the Hebrew language.

Sigismund von Herberstein <note>original: "Sigismond Liber", refers to the diplomat and author of *Rerum Moscoviticarum Commentarii* (1549)</note> in his history of Muscovy:

> » Who first ruled the Ruthenians is uncertain. For they lacked characters <note>i.e., a writing system</note> by which their deeds could have been committed to writing. However, after Michael, the Emperor of Constantinople, sent Slavonic letters into Bulgaria in the year of the World 6406 <note>Using the Byzantine calendar, this corresponds to approximately 898 AD, though Cyril and Methodius's mission was earlier in the 860s</note>, then for the first time, not only those things then occurring, but also those they had received from their ancestors and held through long memory, began to be written down and recorded in their annals.

The same author, speaking of the Vandals, says:

> » The Vandals were powerful in that time, and they used the language, customs, and religion of the Ruthenians; thus it seems to me that the Ruthenians called forth their Princes from the Wagrians, or rather the Varangians <note>original: "Vuaregis", referring to the Viking-led Rus'</note>, rather than conferring power upon foreigners who differed from them in religion, customs, and idiom.

The Christian Russians of the Greek Church sing their Mass and celebrate the divine service in their vernacular tongue, and are subject in spiritual matters to the Patriarch of Constantinople.

### Of the language of the Muscovites.

**N**ICOLAS Chalcondyle <note>Laonikos Chalkokondyles (c. 1423–1490), a Byzantine historian</note> in book 3 of his history of the Turks, describing the customs and ways of the Muscovites, asserts that for the most part they use the Slavonic language, and that as for their customs and ways, even in what depends on Religion, they are Christians, adhering more closely however to the tradition of the Greeks than to the Roman Church and the Pope.

...with whom they are not in good agreement: for they even have a Greek Bishop whom they obey; their households and utensils are hardly different from those of the Tartars.

Matthias of Miechów <note>Matthias Michovius (1457–1523), a Polish scholar, historian, and physician known for his descriptions of Eastern Europe</note>, in book 2, chapter 4 of his *Description of European Sarmatia*, says these words about the Muscovite language: <note>original: "Accipiat Lector in Moschouia vnam linguam & vnum sermonem esse, scilicet Ruthenicum, seu Sclauonicum..."</note> "Let the reader understand that in Muscovy there is one language and one speech, namely Ruthenian or Slavonic, in all the provinces and principalities, so that even the people of Uglich <note>original: "Ohulici"</note> and those who live in Vyatka <note>original: "Viathca"</note> are Ruthenians and speak Ruthenian; they hold to one sect and religion like the Greeks. All the Vladikas <note>original: "Vladicæ", a term used for Eastern Orthodox bishops</note>, of whom there are many, are subject to the Patriarch of Constantinople and, seeking confirmation from him, they promise obedience. This excludes the Tartars of Kazan <note>original: "Coſnenſes aut Coſanenſes"</note>, who, while acknowledging the Duke of Muscovy, worship Muhammad alongside the Saracens and speak the language of the Tartars; it also excludes the foreigners living to the North in Scythia <note>A classical term used here for the remote regions of Northern Eurasia</note>, who speak their own speeches and languages and worship idols, as will be discussed in the following chapter."

The same author in chapter 5 continues with these words:

> "Beyond Muscovy are nations and regions between the North and the East at the edge of Northern Asia, which is properly called Scythia. These are subject to the Prince of Muscovy, having been primarily subjugated by Ivan, Duke of Muscovy: namely Perm, Bashkir <note>original: "Baſlzird"</note>, Cheremis <note>original: "Czriremisſa", referring to the Mari people</note>, Yugra <note>original: "Iuhra"</note>, and Karelia <note>original: "Corela"</note>. 'Perm' is a single syllable, hence the land is called 'Permska,' pronouncing it with two syllables. It was a region that worshipped idols, which Ivan, Duke of the Muscovites, forced to receive baptism less than 20 years ago, according to the custom of the Ruthenians or Greeks. He appointed for them a Vladika, that is, a Bishop, named Stephen, whom the barbarians flayed alive and killed after the Duke's departure. Upon his return, the Duke punished them and appointed another prelate again, under whom they remain as new Christians, professing the schism and rite of the Ruthenians. However, the other regions mentioned persist in infidelity and idolatry. They worship the Sun, Moon, stars, forest beasts, and whatever they encounter. They have their own languages and idioms. In the land of Permska there is a proper idiom, in the land of the Bashkirs their own, in Yugra their own, and in Karelia also their own. In these regions they do not plow, they do not sow, they have no bread nor money; they feed on the wild beasts of the forests, which abound among them, and they drink nothing but water. They dwell in thick forests, in huts made of brushwood. And because the forests covered those lands, they have made the men wild and beast-like."

Sebastian Münster <note>A German cartographer and Hebraist (1488–1552) whose "Cosmographia" was a highly influential geographical work</note>, in book 4 of his *Universal Cosmography*, in the chapter on Muscovy, describing this region at length, says these words about the language of the Muscovites: "The language they have is Slavonic; however, it is so mixed <note>original: "confus", here meaning mingled or diverged</note> with foreign languages that the Slavonic and the Muscovite speakers cannot understand one another. Muscovy extends as far as Yugra and Karelia, which are in Scythia." Paolo Giovio <note>Paulus Jovius (1483–1552), an Italian physician and historian who wrote about the first Muscovite embassy to Rome</note>, in his short book on the embassy of the Muscovites, treating extensively the region of Muscovy, its religion, and the ways of life of its people, makes mention of their language in these words: <note>original: "Moschouitæ Illyrica lingua, Illyricísque literis vtuntur..."</note> "The Muscovites use the Illyrian language and Illyrian letters <note>A historical term for the Cyrillic alphabet and Slavic languages</note>, just as do the Slavs, Dalmatians, Bohemians, Poles, and Lithuanians. This language is said to be by far the most widespread of all; for in Constantinople it is familiar in the Court of the Ottomans, and..."

This same Jovius <note>Paolo Giovio (1483–1552), an Italian physician and historian who wrote about Muscovy</note>, in the place cited above, mentioning the sacred books which these Muscovites use in their religion, says: ”The history of the life and all the miracles of Christ written by the four Evangelists, and likewise the Epistles of Saint Paul, are recited from a higher pulpit with a clear voice during the holy rites. Priests of proven life read publicly the homilies of the doctors of the Church, even during those hours when the sacraments are not being performed. For they do not believe it right to admit hooded orators <note>A reference to monks or friars</note> who are accustomed to preaching to the assembled people and to discourse too ambitiously and subtly about divine matters. These men of solid religion believe that the unlearned minds of the ignorant reach a holier state of morals through simple doctrine rather than through the deepest interpretations of mysteries. <note>original: "nō enim Oratores cuculla os... fimplici potius doctrinā, quàm altiffimis arcanorū interpretationibus"</note> These sacred books we just mentioned, as well as commentators on the New and Old Testament—and furthermore Ambrose, Augustine, Jerome, and Gregory <note>The four Great Doctors of the Western Church</note>—they have translated into the Illyrian language <note>term: Illyrian|Here used as a general term for the Slavic or Slavonic language</note> and religiously preserve. The prelates and chiefs of the minor priests in each city and the prefects of the villages care for the sacred rites and settle controversies, and they pursue those of depraved morals with a certain supreme power of punishment. The king of the sacred rites, whom they call the Metropolitan <note>term: Metropolitan|An archbishop or high-ranking bishop in Eastern Christianity</note>, they seek from the Patriarch of Constantinople.” Sigismund von Herberstein <note>original: "Sigifmond Liber", author of 'Rerum Moscoviticarum Commentarii' (1549)</note> in his *Commentaries on Muscovite Matters* writes the same. André Thevet <note>A French Franciscan priest and explorer</note>, in book 19, chapter 9 of his *Universal Cosmography*, treats at length the language of the aforementioned Muscovites and Permians <note>People from the Perm region of Russia</note>, having imitated or rather followed everything we cited above from Matthias of Miechów in his *European Sarmatia*.

Sigismund von Herberstein, in his *Commentary on Muscovite Matters*, speaking of the aforementioned Muscovite language, which is none other, according to him, than the Slavonic language, says: ”The Slavonic language, which today is somewhat corruptly called 'Sclauonica,' is very widely extended; for it is used by the Dalmatians, Bosnians, Croatians, and Istrians along a long stretch of the Adriatic Sea as far as Friuli, and by the Carni, whom the Venetians call 'Charsi.' Also the Carniolans and Carinthians as far as the Drava River; the Styrians below Graz, along the Mur as far as the Danube, and from there the Moesians, Serbs, Bulgarians, and others living as far as Constantinople. Furthermore, it is used by the Bohemians, Lusatians, Silesians, Moravians, and those living by the Váh river in the kingdom of Hungary; likewise the Poles, and the Ruthenians <note>term: Ruthenians|A historical term for East Slavs, primarily ancestors of modern Ukrainians and Belarusians</note> who rule very widely, and the Circassians of the Five Mountains near the Black Sea; and finally, throughout Germany beyond the Elbe to the North, the remnants of the Vandals <note>original: "Vuandalorum reliquiæ", referring to the Wends, a Slavic people in Germany</note> living scattered about use it. Although all these acknowledge they are Slavs, the Germans, taking the name from the Vandals alone, call everyone using the Slavonic language 'Wenden,' 'Winden,' and 'Windisch' indiscriminately.” <note>original: "Slauonica lingua quæ hodierno die corruptè nonnihil Sclauonica appellatur... Vuendem, Vuinden & Vuindisch promifcuè appellant."</note>

The same author, speaking of the Mordvins <note>original: "Mordues"</note>, or Morduues, people subject to the Grand Duke of Muscovy: ”Towards the East and South from the Moskva River, one encounters vast forests inhabited by the Mordvin people, who use their own idiom and are subject to the Prince of Muscovy. Some would have them be idolaters, others Muslims.” <note>original: "A Mofcha fluuio Orientem & Meridiem verfus... Eos quidem idololatras, alij Mahometanos effe volunt."</note>

...had stayed with them, yet even then those present could still recognize their words. <note>original: "moratus cum eis fuerat, adhuc tamen tunc præsentes verba illorum deprehendere poterant."</note> This same person later said, they have gymnasiums <note>In this context, schools for higher learning or classical education</note>, though few, in which the children of the nobility are instructed in good literature, and especially in sacred matters, most frequently in the Ruthenian language <note>The author uses "Ruthenian" to refer to the Old East Slavic or Russian language</note>; there are very few who apply themselves to foreign languages. Most devote themselves to Greek because of the writings <note>original: "monumenta"</note> of the holy fathers Chrysostom, Nazianzen, Basil, and the others, and for the sake of all those things derived from the Greeks that can be adapted to their customs or region. They entirely neglect Hebrew, except for this single word *Alleluia*, which is commonly used in the Mass. Matthew, Mark, Luke, John, the Epistles of Paul, and the others received by us along with the Apocalypse [Revelation], are counted among the canonical Scriptures of the New Testament. Concerning the canonical books of the Old Testament, they assert the same as the Catholic Church has decreed. They recognize the Roman Pontiff as the Vicar of Christ and the successor of Peter; for this reason, the feasts of Saint Clement, Saint Leo, and Saint Gregory are customarily celebrated among the Muscovites.

To be brief, we shall say that the historians of the Greek Empire, according to the words of the aforementioned Sigismund von Herberstein <note>original: "Sigismōd Liber," referring to the Austrian diplomat whose "Commentaries on Muscovite Affairs" (1549) was the primary Western source on Russia at the time</note> in his *Commentaries on Muscovite Affairs*, hold that the Muscovites (who are none other than the Russians) used no characters or letters to write and record their deeds and actions before the Empire of Michael the Paphlagonian <note>Michael IV, Byzantine Emperor from 1034 to 1041</note>, Emperor of Greece, under whom in the Year of the World 6406 <note>Using the Byzantine calendar, this corresponds to approximately 898 AD</note>, they adapted themselves to the language and characters of the Sclavons <note>Slavs</note>, from whom they claim to originate, notwithstanding that their princes boast of being descended from the Romans. The aforementioned Muscovites assert in their histories that it is very difficult to know for certain who were the first to make themselves Lords and commanders in Muscovy, Lithuania, and White Russia, and that the cause of such ignorance came from the fact that the peoples of these regions used no written letters to record the deeds of their Kings and states. They also claim that many of the ancients had no true knowledge of these regions, seeing the errors and lies found in their history books; but that in the time of the aforementioned Greek Emperor Michael the Paphlagonian, they learned the letters and characters of the aforementioned Sclavons [Slavs], which was also the reason they learned their language. For this Emperor sent people to instruct them in the Year of Salvation 136 <note>The text says 136, but this is likely a chronological error or a typo for 1036, which would fall within Michael IV's reign</note>; consequently, there have been only sixty-some years <note>This "sixty years" likely reflects the perspective of the original source used by the author, rather than the author’s own time</note> since these Muscovites have had knowledge of letters. It is true that they then recorded in writing in their Russian language what they had learned from father to son and retained from long memory concerning their antiquity and that of their princes. See what André Thevet <note>A 16th-century French Franciscan priest, explorer, and cosmographer</note> has detailed extensively on this matter in Book 19, Chapter 11 and following of his *Universal Cosmography*.

the one who has several Dukes under his obedience is called *Vueliki Knest* <note>original: "Vueliki Knest," a transliteration of the Russian "Veliky Knyaz"</note>, which is to say, Grand Dukes.

The aforementioned Muscovites also call their Grand Duke *Kzar* <note>Tsar</note>, which in the Russian language means King, but in Slavonic, Polish, Hungarian, and Bohemian, its meaning carries as much weight as Emperor or Caesar: for *Crall*, or *kirail* <note>Hungarian: "Király"</note>, means to them as much as King does to us. Some peoples call him the White King in Slavonic: because just as the Sophy of Persia <note>The Safavid Shah</note> is called *Kusilpassa*, or *Cuselbas* or *Caselbas* <note>Qizilbash, meaning "Red-heads," referring to their headgear</note>, because the Royal ornament he wears on his head is red, so too the Muscovite is called white, because the Royal ornament he wears on his head is of that color. This Duke takes the name of King when writing to anyone except the King of Poland, as I have already said, but there is no one who honors him with the title of King, except for some of his own people and those of Livonia, because no High Pontiff <note>the Pope</note> nor Emperor has crowned him King, as has happened to those who currently bear that honorable title. And when those who call him such are asked the reason for it, they respond that the Royal name is well-deserved by him since other Kings are his tributaries.

Sigismund Herberstein <note>Sigismund von Herberstein (1486–1566), a diplomat for the Holy Roman Empire</note> has written on this subject in his *Commentaries on Muscovite Affairs* the following words, worthy of being recited in full in this place.

> » <note>The following passage was originally in Latin</note> He uses his authority in both spiritual and secular matters; he freely and by his own will disposes of the lives and goods of everyone. Among the counselors he has, none is of such authority that they would dare to disagree or resist him in any matter. They publicly declare that the will of the Prince is the will of God, and whatever the Prince does, he does by the will of God; for this reason, they also call him the key-bearer and chamberlain of God, and they believe him to be the executor of the divine will. Hence the Prince himself, whenever prayers are offered for some prisoner or another grave matter, is accustomed to answer: "When God commands it, he shall be released." Likewise, if anyone asks about some uncertain or doubtful matter, they commonly answer: "God and the Great Prince know." It is uncertain whether the great ferocity of the people requires a tyrannical Prince, or whether by the tyranny of the Prince, the people themselves are rendered so fierce, hard, and cruel.

> » From the time of Rurik until this present Prince, those princes used no other title than Grand Dukes of either Vladimir, or Moscow, or Novgorod, etc., except for Ivan Vasilyevich <note>Ivan III</note>, who called himself Lord of all Russia and Grand Duke of Vladimir, etc. But this Vasily Ivanovich <note>Vasily III</note> claims for himself both the title and the name of King in this manner: "The Great Lord Vasily, by the grace of God King and Lord of all Russia, and Grand Duke of Vladimir, Moscow, Novgorod, Pskov, Smolensk, Tver, Yugra, Perm, Vyatka, Bulgaria, etc. Lord and Grand Duke of Lower Novgorod <note>Nizhny Novgorod</note>, and of Chernigov, Ryazan, Volokolamsk, Rzhev, Bely, Rostov, Yaroslavl, Belozersk, Udoria, Obdoria, Kondia, etc." Furthermore, since everyone now calls him "Emperor," it seems necessary that I explain both the title and the cause of this error. *Czar* in the Ruthenian <note>Russian</note> language signifies King, but in the common Slavonic language used among the Poles, Bohemians, and all others—taking a certain resonance from the last and heavy syllable—"Czar" is understood as Emperor or Caesar. Thus, all those who are not skilled in the Ruthenian idiom or letters...

" The Bohemians, Poles, and even the Slavs subject to the Kingdom of Hungary, call a King by another name, namely: *Kral*, others *Kyrall*, and some *Koroll*. They believe that *Czar* refers only to Caesar or the Emperor: hence it happened that the Ruthenian <note>A historical term for the East Slavic people of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and Russia</note> interpreters, hearing their Prince called this by foreign nations, began to call him Emperor themselves, and subsequently they considered the name *Czar* to be more dignified than that of King, even though they signify the same thing. Furthermore, if you examine all their histories and the Holy Scripture, you will find the name *Czar* used for King, while *Kessar* is used for Emperor. By the same error, the Emperor of the Turks is called *Czar*, who nevertheless has anciently used no title more eminent than that of King, which is to say, *Czar*. Hence the European Turks who use the Slavonic language call Constantinople *Czarigrad*, as if to say the Royal City. There are those who call this Prince of Muscovy the White King. I have indeed diligently sought the reason why he is called by the name of the White King, since none of the Princes of Muscovy had used that title before: indeed, when the occasion arose, I spoke openly to the Councilors themselves, saying that we recognize him not as King, but as the Grand Duke. Many, however, thought the reason for this Royal name was that he had Kings under his empire: but elsewhere this reason held no weight. I believe, however—just as they now call the Persians *Kusilpassa* <note>original: "Kusilpassa," referring to the Qizilbash, meaning "Red-head"</note>, which is to say "Red Head," because of their red head-coverings—that they are called "White" because of their white head-coverings. Furthermore, he uses the title of King when writing to the Roman Emperor and the Pope, the King of Sweden, and Denmark, and the Masters of Prussia and Livonia, etc. And as I have heard, he uses it with the Prince of the Turks; yet he himself is called King by none of these, except perhaps by the Livonians. In ancient times, they were accustomed to use titles enclosed within three circles in a triangle, of which the first in the topmost circle contained these words: *Our God is the Trinity, who was before all ages, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, yet not three Gods, but one God in substance.* In the second was the title of the Emperor of the Turks, with the added phrase *To our beloved Brother.* In the third was the title of the Grand Duke of Muscovy, by which he declared himself King and heir and lord of all Eastern and Southern Russia, in which we saw the common formula added: *We have sent to you our faithful Councilor.* Toward the King of Poland, the Grand Lord Basil <note>Grand Prince Vasily III (ruled 1505–1533)</note> uses this kind of title: *By the grace of God, Lord of all Russia, and Grand Duke of Vladimir, Moscow, Novgorod, Smolensk, Tver, Yugra, Perm, Bulgaria, etc.,* omitting the title of King. For neither of these deigns to receive letters from the other enhanced with a new title; which indeed happened while we were in Muscovy, when the Muscovite received with difficulty the letters of King Sigismund sent to him, which were enhanced with the title of Duke of Masovia. Some write that the Muscovite sought the name and Royal title from the Roman Pope and the Emperor Maximilian; this does not seem likely to me, especially since he considers himself inferior to no man, even the High Pontiff, whom he deigns to call only by the title of "Doctor" <note>This implies the ruler viewed the Pope as a mere teacher or scholar rather than a sovereign or spiritual superior</note>. Furthermore, he does not consider the Roman Emperor to be greater than himself, as appears from his letters, in which he places his own name before the title of Emperor. Likewise, the name for "Duke" among them is called *Knes*: nor did they ever have another greater title, as I said, except by adding that word, "Grand." For all others who held a single principality were called *Knes*: but those who held several principalities and had other *Knes* subject under their Empire were called *Vueliki Knesi*, that is, Grand Dukes. They have no other rank or dignity after the *Boiaros* <note>The Boyars, the highest rank of the Slavic nobility</note>, who in our manner hold the place of nobles or knights. In Croatia, the leaders are similarly called *Knesi*.

### *Of the Region of the Goths.*

Abraham Ortelius <note>A famous Flemish cartographer and geographer</note>, in his *Geographical Synonyms and Treasury*, identifies the <gloss>Getai</gloss> <note>original Greek: "γέται"</note> as the
Peoples of European Sarmatia, called Dacians by the Romans, as attested by Strabo
and Pliny. Spartianus, in his life of Caracalla, is the authority for calling the Goths "Getai."
Strabo says that the Getai live on both banks of the Danube, toward the Black Sea and the East,
and Ovid confirms this. Stephanus also places the region of Getia in Thrace.
The same author records that the Getai are called *Getinos* by Arrian; Bonfinius
writes that they are called Wallachians today. Arias Montanus records that the
Getai and Massagetae are called Magog by the Hebrews. Vignier
teaches that Goths and Getai are synonyms for a single nation, and that they
inhabited European Scythia between the Black Sea and the Danube. See Dacia and Scythia.

The Goths, on the northern side of the Black Sea, were called *Polouci* by their neighbors,
which in the Ruthenian language means "robbers" and "plunderers," according to Matthew
of Miechów. Stephanus writes "Goths" as <gloss>Gothoi</gloss> <note>original Greek: "γότθοι"</note> with a *tau* and a *theta*. The Goths are mentioned in the Panegyric addressed to the Emperor Maximian.
Cedrenus also mentions the Hypogoths. Hadrianus Junius, in chapter 23
of his *Batavia*, writes that the Goths were called *Trolos* by the Vandals; see Getai.

Gothia <gloss>Gothia</gloss> <note>original Greek: "γότθια"</note> is an Archiepiscopal seat in the Sanctions of the
Eastern Pontiffs. The Metropolis of the Province of Gothia is mentioned in the Council of Nicaea <note>The first ecumenical council of the Christian church, held in 325 AD</note>;
its Bishop was Theophilus. I believe this was in Gaul. See Dacia, Guta, Rome,
Narbonnese Gaul, Septimania, and Zicchia.

### Of the Goths.

Johannes Magnus <note>A 16th-century Swedish archbishop and historian</note>, in the first book of his *Northern Histories*: <margin>“</margin> "The first seat of the Goths in Scythia <note>An ancient region of Eurasia</note> was most notable near the Pontic Sea <note>The Black Sea</note>; <margin>“</margin> from there the name of the Nation became more famous, and from there they were called 'Scythiæ', that is, <margin>“</margin> victors over the Scythians <note>original Latin: *Scytharum victores*</note>. However, I do not deny that they themselves were afterwards sometimes <margin>“</margin> called Scythians, and sometimes Goths or Getæ <note>An ancient Thracian tribe often conflated with the Goths</note>. Indeed, according to the diversity of <margin>“</margin> languages over which they ruled—just as in their native land they were called 'Vestro-gothæ', <margin>“</margin> that is Western Getæ, and 'Ostrogetæ', that is Eastern—so too in foreign <margin>“</margin> lands and foreign tongues, they were called now Samagetæ, now Massagetæ (whom Strabo, <margin>“</margin> in book 11, affirms are Eastern Goths), and finally Tirsagetæ. Therefore, <margin>“</margin> both Greeks and Latins not infrequently named these Goths interchangeably <margin>“</margin> within the same nation. And Paul Orosius <note>A 5th-century historian</note> in his first book testifies to the same. <margin>“</margin> 'Presently,' he says, 'those Getæ, who are now also Goths—whom Alexander [the Great] announced <margin>“</margin> should be avoided, whom Pyrrhus dreaded, and whom Caesar even <margin>“</margin> turned away from.' Furthermore, Procopius <note>A 6th-century Byzantine historian</note> says regarding Vitiges <note>King of the Ostrogoths</note> besieging Rome: <margin>“</margin> 'At that time the Roman Patricians brought forth the sayings of the Sibyl <note>Prophetic oracles</note>, <margin>“</margin> asserting that the city would be in danger until the month of July, and finally <margin>“</margin> that Rome should fear nothing Getic.' For they affirm these to be the 'Getic' <margin>“</margin> nation of the Goths, as do many other ancient and more recent authors, such as Dio the Greek <note>Cassius Dio</note>, who entitled his histories with a title concerning Getic matters." <margin>“</margin>

Furthermore, Jordanes the Goth <note>A 6th-century historian of the Goths</note> in his history calls them now *Cothi*, now *Getæ*. And Paul the Deacon <note>An 8th-century historian of the Lombards</note> affirms they are *Gothogetæ* in his *Life of Narses*. Olaus <note>Likely Olaus Magnus, brother of Johannes Magnus</note> on page 245 [writes]: "If my experience merits any trust, I can testify that I am called *Ostrogeta* by my fellow Goths, while I am called *Ostro-Gothus* by the Latins: for from the most ancient times in our homeland we call that *Getha* which Latin speech is accustomed to call *Gothus*." Nor does Herodotus, the father of history, disagree with this interchangeable naming; he asserts that the Massagetæ (that is, the Ostrogoths) drove the Scythians from their seats, and then proceeding, drove out the Cimmerian inhabitants and held their lands. This is also testified by Raphael Volaterranus <note>Raffaele Maffei, a 15th-century humanist</note> in book 7, citing Strabo and Homer, who affirms in the *Odyssey*, book 10, that they arrived from the furthest West. No one well-versed in history is ignorant of how true this is regarding the Goths occupying Cimmeria <note>The region of the Crimea</note>. Ptolemy also confirms this view, saying that the Massagetæ settled in the inland parts of Asia, in the region of the Scythians. Therefore, unless the prudent reader notices that the Goths and Getæ are the same people—and that they were sometimes called Scythians, sometimes Cimmerians, or Thracians by the nations they conquered—he will never understand Gothic or Scythian history. Indeed, while King Filimer was still alive after they had driven out the Cimmerians, they were called not only Cimmerians but also Scythians, having obtained the name from the land they occupied. Herodotus, following this victory, says they were not content with driving the Cimmerians from their homes, but asserts they followed those who had fled with such force and fury that they could not distinguish the path they were to take, etc.

B. de Vigenère <note>Blaise de Vigenère, a French diplomat and scholar</note> in his *Treatise on Ciphers*, leaf 534, has described very particularly the history of these Goths, and of their travels and conquests.

<page-num>860</page-num>
<header>HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF / Of the Language of the Goths.</header>

A certain Archbishop of Toledo <note>Likely referring to Rodrigo Jiménez de Rada (c. 1170–1247), a Spanish bishop and historian</note> believed—though without evidence or cause—that the Gothic alphabet was the first of all alphabets and the most ancient letters, given by God at the beginning of the world to our first Father, Adam. Saint **Jerome** <note>original: "Hierosme"</note> completely contradicts this in chapter 9 of his commentary on the Prophet **Ezekiel**, saying that in the ancient books of the Samaritans, the letter *Tau* had the form of a cross. This cannot be reconciled with the shape of the Gothic letter 'T'. This matter is treated at great length by **Goropius Becanus** in books 5 and 16 of his *Hieroglyphics*, by **Sixtus Senensis** in book 2 of his *Holy Library*, and by **Alanus Copus** in his *Dialogues against the Heretics*, book 4, chapter 10. Regarding this, **F. Louys Portugaiz** <note>Friar Luis of Portugal</note> writes in book 1, chapter 1 of his *Globe of Canons and Secrets of the Holy Language and Divine Scripture*:
» <note>original Latin: *Vnde iam manifestissimè apparet...*</note> "From which it now most clearly appears that the most reverend Lord Salicæus, Archbishop of Toledo, was mistaken when he thought the alphabet of Gothic letters was the first alphabet and the first characters given to the first parent [Adam]. The authority of Saint Jerome on chapter 9 of Ezekiel provides him no support at all; Jerome says that in the ancient books of the Samaritans, the *Tau* bore a resemblance to a cross, but Saint Jerome is by no means speaking of the Gothic letter 'T', but of the ancient Hebrew letter, which indeed represents a sign and the Cross of Christ."

Northern histories hold that a certain **Ulfilas** <note>original: "Vulphilas" or "Gulphila"</note>, a Goth by nation and Bishop of Gothia—the successor of **Theophilus** who lived under the Arian Emperor **Valens**—was initially Orthodox. (Of him, **Socrates** in book 4, chapter 33 of his *Ecclesiastical History*, **Sozomen** in book 6, chapter 34, and the *Tripartite History* in book 8, chapter 13, speak at length.) He was the first to invent letters and characters for those of his nation, and the first who translated the Holy Scriptures from the Greek language into his Gothic tongue, explaining them to the people in a purely Catholic <note>Here meaning "universal" or "orthodox" rather than specifically Roman Catholic, as Ulfilas is historically associated with the Arian sect</note> manner. This is confirmed by **Sixtus Senensis** in book 4 of his *Holy Library*.

On the contrary, **Johannes Magnus** <note>original: "Iean le Grand"</note> writes that the Goths made use of these letters and characters attributed to the aforementioned **Ulfilas** long before his time. However, he does confess that this figure was the first to use them in a version of the Holy Scriptures which he produced; for this reason, he was reputed to have been the first inventor of letters and characters among the Goths. Some historians hold that the Goths have had their own characters and letters since ancient times to write whatever they wished, such that children learning their letters were simultaneously led to commit to memory certain verses made in honor of their gods and of illustrious men who had performed some high and excellent exploit for the defense of their country and nation. And not only children, but also men of distinction, who, by virtue of this duty and by showing themselves learned and curious in such research, earned Kingdoms and dignities and were placed among the number of the gods.

**Johannes Magnus**, in book 1 of his *Northern History*, the chapter on Gothic letters:
» <note>original Latin: *Credendum non est...*</note> "It is not to be believed that the Northerners themselves were entirely without writers of their own magnificently performed deeds, since long before Latin letters were invented, and before Carmenta <note>A Roman goddess of childbirth and prophecy, credited in myth with inventing the Latin alphabet</note> [arrived] from Greece at the mouth of the Tiber and Roman soil..."

> <note>original: "...Euandro perueniſſet, expulſiſque Aboriginibus gentem illam rudem mo- res & literas docuiſſet Gothi ſuas literas habuerint..."</note> ...[when he] had arrived with **Evander** <note>In Roman mythology, a hero from Arcadia who brought Greek culture and the alphabet to Italy</note>, and having driven out the **Aborigines** <note>The earliest native inhabitants of central Italy</note>, he had taught that rude people customs and letters, the **Goths** already had their own letters. Evidence of this matter is provided by stones of extraordinary size, fixed to the tombs and caves of the ancient Goths: which, being inscribed with the forms of letters, might persuade one that they had been erected there by Giant-like strength before the universal flood, or shortly thereafter. Expressing their deeds on stones with these characters, they handed them down to the eternal memory of men. Although they lacked knowledge of the Roman speech—which at that time, before the founding of Rome, did not exist—nevertheless, such a great diligence for the study of eloquence and for writing their native poems inflamed them, so that not only modest boys (as **Cato** writes the Romans did much later) were everywhere instructed to sing ancient songs in which the praises of their ancestors were contained, but even grave men sang to the flutes about the virtues of famous men (as is still done today): and so great was the honor and reward of learning, that most people bestowed not only scepters and kingdoms but even divine honors upon the wise.
> cc

**Olaus Magnus** <note>A Swedish ecclesiastic and writer (1490–1557) famous for his descriptions of Northern peoples</note>, brother of the aforementioned **John** <note>Johannes Magnus (1488–1544), Archbishop of Uppsala, who wrote a history of the Goths and Swedes</note>, writes the following in Book 1, Chapter 36 of his histories of the **Northern Peoples**:

> <note>original: "Ab antiquiſſimo tempore cùm eſſent Gigantes in Septentrion. terris..."</note> From the most ancient times, when there were Giants in the Northern lands—that is, long before Latin letters were invented, and before **Carmenta** <note>A goddess of childbirth and prophecy, mother of Evander, credited with inventing the Latin alphabet</note> came from Greece to the mouths of the Tiber and the Roman soil with Evander, and, having expelled the Aborigines, taught that rude and clearly woodland people customs and letters—the Northern kingdoms had their own letters. Evidence of this matter is provided by stones of extraordinary size fixed to the tombs and caves of the ancients. If anyone doubts whether these were produced by Giants and in a most ancient age, let him go there and see things larger and more wondrous to the point of amazement than any writing might promise or provide. Thus, with these (as is held in the history of my dearest brother **John Magnus**, predecessor Archbishop of **Uppsala** <note>original: "Vſpalenſis"</note>, Book 1, Chapter 52), impressing their deeds on stones, they handed them down to eternal memory. Some also used various figures of animals as letters for private accounts, after the fashion of the Egyptians, and they still use them with domestic sagacity, as will be said shortly below: similar ones can still be seen in Rome on ancient obelisks, in which individual letters expressed individual names—for instance, a wolf for a greedy man, a fox for a cunning one, a bee for a King: because it behooves a ruler of peoples to have the honey of mercy mixed with the sting of justice. Furthermore, just as letters inscribed on papyrus are now sent between men, so once the Northern inhabitants sent letters carved on wood as a celebrated kind of paper: indeed, even now when papyrus is not available, in military camps or during the siege of cities, they opportunely use the bark or the inner wood of the birch tree split into sheets—indeed, into thin leaves—for writing letters, and all the more securely because bark of this kind is not destroyed by any injury of rain or snow. **Peter Martyr** <note>Pietro Martire d'Anghiera (1457–1526), an Italian-born historian of Spain's explorations</note> also mentions in Book 8 that the **Chaldeans** now write on the leaves of trees, and that the first **Portuguese** discoverers of the **New World** used them when they were forced to restore mutual defenses to suppress the rebellion of the inhabitants. Northern men are also found of such sagacious intellect that, although they have never learned either Gothic or Latin letters, they compose alphabets for themselves from the figures of things and tools: and for the sake of assisting their memory, on skin, paper...

<page-num>863</page-num>
<header>LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE.</header>

As for their language, no traces of it are found from which one could speak with certainty; however, the Letters of Cassiodorus <note>Secretary to the Ostrogothic King Theodoric the Great</note>, Secretary to Theodoric, teach us that in their public acts they used the Latin language. It is true that the *Histories of Spain* assert that the Gothic language was entirely similar to the language of the Celts. Others affirm that it was the same Teutonic language, the relics of which corrupted languages are today much more different than they possibly were during their period of greatest purity; this is confirmed by Louis de Mayerne Turquet in Book 5 of his *History of Spain*.

Olaus Magnus, cited above in Book 8, Chapter 2 of his *Northern Histories*, writes that the Goths have a certain book written in their language titled *billagines* <note>A term used by the historian Jordanes to describe the ancient laws of the Goths</note>, which was composed by one of their kings named Deceneus, who in his time was the first to teach his people the Philosophy and Religion of Pythagoras. Now, this word *billagines* signifies, according to the report of the aforementioned Olaus in the Gothic language, the same as in Latin, *according to the laws* <note>original: "iuxta leges"</note>. See what this same author writes in Book 1, Chapter 34 of his same histories concerning certain staffs engraved with Gothic letters, by which the Goths from all antiquity served themselves in the knowledge of Astronomy, and to predict and announce the events of times and seasons, and to know the movable feasts and dominical letters <note>Letters used in calendars to determine the day of the week for any given date</note> of future years.

Furthermore, it seems to me very appropriate to mention in this place that the *Histories of Spain* state that when Don Sancho Ramírez <note>King of Aragon and later Navarre (r. 1063–1094)</note> came to the crown of Navarre, he had already reigned in Aragon for several years; he had married a lady, the daughter of the Count of Urgel, named Lady Felicia, by whom he had three children. Under this Prince, the two kingdoms of Navarre and Aragon were reunited 42 years after their separation. He was a warrior and a statesman, and furthermore was a zealot for the Roman Religion. For he caused the Gothic office <term>office des Goths: The Mozarabic or Visigothic Rite, a Christian liturgy distinct from the Roman Rite that persisted in Spain for centuries</term>, which the Christians used in his lands, to be changed, and put the Roman rite into use; possibly by the Council held at Jaca under this King, when the Bishopric of Aragon was first established. For the adornment and enrichment of this see, besides the tithes, portions of the conquests made against the Moors of Zaragoza and Tudela were ordained; and in place of the Gothic civil laws, he introduced the Common Imperial Law into his jurisdiction. There is even a volume of particular laws given by this King to those of Jaca, which is inserted among the customs and usages of Navarre today.

The same histories continue that at this same time mention is made of a Council assembled in the city of Barcelona at the pursuit of Don Ramon Berenguer the Elder, at the request of Lady Almodis his wife, over which presided Cardinal Hugh, Legate of Pope Alexander II or Gregory VII—for the time of it is not precisely fixed, but it is only said that it was celebrated around the year 1071. At this Council, it was ordained that the clergy should live chastely, for as much as, the history says, several ecclesiastics were married, according to the introduction of King Wittiza the Goth <note>The last Visigothic king before the Umayyad conquest, often blamed by later chroniclers for the moral decline of the kingdom</note>, and following the example of the Aragonese, [the office] was left [behind]...

the Mozarabic rite, and received the Roman rite of Saint Gregory in the lands of Catalonia.

The same Histories continue that in the year 1086, during the reign of Don Alfonso, King of Castile and Navarre, the rite named Gothic—or Isidorean, because Saint Isidore <note>Saint Isidore of Seville (c. 560–636), a scholar and cleric who helped standardize the Spanish liturgy</note> had introduced it, and afterwards called Mozarabic, because the Christians living among the Moors had retained and celebrated it—was in use until that time, both in Toledo and in Castile and Leon. But this King Alfonso, desiring in everything to show himself an affectionate son of the See of Rome, wanted it to be changed, and in its place received the rite called Gregorian, from its author Gregory. Therefore, he sent for a bull from the Pope then reigning, commanding that the Roman rite should henceforth be celebrated in all the Churches of Spain, just as was done in France, because of which it is called by some Spaniards "Gallican." During the time of the aforementioned King, a Council was held at Leon, in the presence of Rainier, the Papal Nuncio, in which among other ordinances it was decreed that copyists and writers would no longer use the ancient Gothic characters invented, as they say, by Ulfilas their Bishop <note>Ulfilas (c. 311–383) was a Goth of Greek descent who translated the Bible into the Gothic language and created the Gothic alphabet</note> (otherwise called Toledan letters), but rather the letters that are currently used in Castile. ->Of the Gothic Philosophers.<-

The Gothic Philosophers, among those of their Nation, were called Zorobes, Terées, and Pileates <note>These terms, derived from the historian Jordanes, refer to different ranks of the Gothic social and intellectual elite; the 'Pileati' or 'hat-wearers' were the noble class</note>; and from among these, the Goths were accustomed to elect their Kings and also their Priests, as well as the Ethespantes, Hauales, Fridigernes, and others of whom Olaus Magnus <note>A 16th-century Swedish ecclesiastic and writer famous for his descriptions of Northern peoples</note> makes ample mention in his *Northern Histories*.

->Of the Region of the Northmen.<-

Abraham Ortelius, in his *Synonyms* and *Geographical Treasury*, says: <note>original: "Dani Populi sunt hodie Denemarker, aut Denemarcker. Apud vetustissimos auctores horum non est mentio. Iornandes eorum primus in historia meminit. Hos eosdem vocant Eginarthus & eius seculi scriptores Northmannos : sed iidem etiam eos sic vocant quos nos hodie Russen vocamus, item Suueden. Dani cum Dacis sæpenumero à iunioribus video confundi, non tamen sine maximo erreur."</note> "The Danish People are today called Danes or Denmarkers. Among the most ancient authors, there is no mention of them. Jordanes was the first to mention them in history. Eginhard <note>A scholar and courtier to Charlemagne</note> and writers of his age call these same people Northmen; but they also use this name for those whom we today call Russians, as well as Swedes. I see the Danes frequently confused with the Dacians <note>An ancient people of the Balkans, often confused with the Danes due to the similarity of the names 'Daci' and 'Dani'</note> by more recent writers, though not without great error."

The Northmen, according to Sigebert and writers of his age, <note>original: "Nortmanni, vocantur à Sigeberto, & eius seculi scriptoribus, omnes fere Septentrionales Gentes ut sunt Noruuegiani, Suediani, & cæteri qui Scandiam peninsulam, atque Russiam incolunt."</note> are the name given to almost all Northern Peoples, such as the Norwegians, Swedes, and others who inhabit the Scandian peninsula and Russia.

Ancient histories hold that after these Northmen had come out of Norway and entered Normandy, they made war for a very long time against the English, and by their ordinary raids they hindered their trade and navigation, and drove out the Saracens <note>A term used in the Middle Ages for Muslims</note> who, having entered Italy, wanted to settle in Calabria and Apulia <note>Regions in southern Italy</note>. Since then, they established colonies in Ireland and Iceland, where those of Brene <note>Likely referring to a specific group or leader mentioned in Norse or Frisian legends</note> had taught them of the discovery that the gentlemen of Frisia <note>A coastal region in the Netherlands and Germany</note> had made of them. Their language itself can serve as proof that they came from Norway: where the old inhabitants still speak like those of Iceland; but now in the maritime places of Norway, and principally where the port of Bergen is, this language has been changed because of the custom and the import of merchants from Germany and Denmark, as is confirmed by the author of the *Thesaurus Politicus* <note>original: "Thresor politique"; a 16th-century collection of political and geographical information</note>, book 3, chapter on Iceland.

### Of the Language of the Franks.

### CHAPTER LXXI.

The Franks—remnants formerly left from the destruction of the Trojans <note>A common medieval legend claimed that European nations were founded by survivors of the Trojan War</note>, some 440 years before the Year of Salvation, or the Incarnation of the Savior—finally came from the large and spacious solitudes of Scythia <note>A vast region in central Eurasia</note>, under the leadership of a Marcomir their chief, to settle in Lower Germany, where their brothers the Saxons granted them a residence toward the mouths of the Rhine, in Frisia and Holland. And from there, making many large incursions into the surrounding lands, they warred against the Romans and Gauls for more than nine hundred whole years. Thus, they extended their domination over the greater part of Europe, as their chronicler Hunibauld <note>A legendary chronicler of the Franks whose work was widely cited in the Renaissance but is now considered mythical</note> amply testifies in the 18 books he left to posterity regarding their conquests. In these, he notes among other things that a certain person named Vuastbal had written their deeds and gestures for 758 years in their own language, and in characters such as we represent hereafter, which feel somewhat like Greek writing: but the order of the letters is transposed, and the rest are a bit doubtful—perhaps because of their great antiquity, which might have caused writers to deprave the true shape, as is confirmed by Abbot Trithemius <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German Benedictine abbot and polymath known for his work on cryptography and history</note> in book 5 of his *Polygraphia*.

## Concerning the region of the Finnonians or Finlanders.

<margin>Abraham Ortelius in his *Synonyms* and *Geographic Treasury*.</margin>
<note>Ortelius (1527–1598) was a famous cartographer who created the first modern atlas.</note>
Tacitus <note>A Roman historian (c. 56–120 AD)</note> doubts whether to assign the Fenni <note>original: "Fenni"</note> to the Germans or the Sarmatians. Althamerus thinks they are Prussians or Lithuanians. Ptolemy <note>A Greek-Roman geographer</note> places the Phinnoi <note>original: "$\phi \acute{\iota} \nu \nu \omicron \iota$"</note> in this region. But it seems to me that the Finni (spelled with an *I* by Jordanes) are rather those who inhabit Finland today. They are in the peninsula of Scandinavia, where there are also the *Scritifini* or *Crictofinni*, though located more toward the North. These are so named from "jumping" in a barbarian tongue, says [Paul] the Deacon. For my part, I derive it from *Scricken* or *Scriien*, a purely Germanic word which signifies to leap or to take great strides with legs spread wide while walking. Indeed, as an eyewitness Olaus <note>Olaus Magnus (1490–1557), a Swedish writer and cartographer</note> testifies, they use wooden soles tied under the plants of their feet: with which they seem to glide through snow and ice with a certain admirable speed, rather than run. The use of these is also found among us during the winter. We call them *Seriekschoenen* <note>An early term for ice skates or skis; original: "Seriekschoenen"</note>, as if you were to say "leaping shoes." It remains to be seen whether, because of this swift running, these same people are those called *Horse-foots* <note>original: "Hippopodes," a mythical tribe mentioned by ancient authors</note> by ancient writers. See under "Vandals."

Modern accounts report that throughout all the provinces of Sweden, Gothia, Norway, and Denmark, there are three different languages in use: namely Swedish (the Saxon language <note>referring to Low German influences</note> closely approaches it in many words, as do Flemish and English, by changing some pronunciation); then there is the Finnish language, which is used not only in the Grand Duchy of Finland (except in one province where Swedish is preserved and practiced, and where "Finland" means as much as "new land"), but also in a good part of the surroundings of Reval <note>modern-day Tallinn, Estonia</note>, a city in Livonia. ### CHAP. LXXIII.

It seemed to me very appropriate to show in this chapter that there is a very great difference between the languages detailed above—German, Polish, Livonian, Swedish, and Finnish—and that they are not alike or similar as some modern figures have believed and asserted. To provide proof of this, we will hereafter include the Lord’s Prayer in each of these languages, by which curious and learned persons may recognize the diversity of each of the aforementioned languages as well as they could through many other discourses in these tongues.

As for what concerns the Finnish or Finlandish language, as it is spoken in the middle of the country, it is in no way aligned with, and shares nothing with the aforementioned Swedish language, nor with the language of the Muscovites <note>The Russians</note>, but it is a language proper to the Lapps <note>The Sámi people</note>, who are a people of the middle of the North.

### The Lord's Prayer in the language of the Lapps and Finns, which is also used by some Livonians.

> Our Father, who art in the heavens, hallowed be Thy name, Thy kingdom come: Thy will be done as in the heavens, so on the ground: give us today our daily bread: and forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who trespass against us: and lead us not into temptation: but deliver us from evil. Amen.
